title: [epic] Metrics catalog + monitoring
description:
Goal: a first-class user-defined METRICS catalog alongside the event catalog, with the same breakdown / app-version / platform splits and the same anomaly monitoring + alerting.

A MetricDefinition mirrors EventType/Event but is defined in one of three KINDS:
- fact_aggregation (GrowthBook-style): fact table / base SELECT + aggregation (count, sum(col), avg, min, max, count_distinct(user)) + optional row filter + breakdowns.
- sql: a user-authored SELECT against a warehouse returning a per-bucket measure.
- event_composition: derived from already-collected event_metrics — single event count, ratio A/B, or A / distinct users.

AGREED DESIGN DECISIONS (2026-06-29, confirmed by product owner):
1. GLOBAL layer, NOT branch-scoped. MetricDefinition has project_id only (no branch_id). NO plan_branch deep-copy/merge/conflict wiring. event_composition references canonical (main-branch) events/event_types.
2. SIMPLE lifecycle: MetricStatus = draft / active / archived (no 7-state machine, no merge-rank).
3. HYBRID collection: sql/fact_aggregation have their own data_source_id + interval and run via the warehouse adapter; event_composition is bound to the source events scan grid and reads event_metrics.
4. distinct-users IN v1: adapter aggregation must include count_distinct; the composition evaluator needs a per-bucket distinct-user denominator series (collected via count_distinct from the warehouse).

REUSE (~80%): clone event_type.py+event.py and event_service.py for the catalog; clone event_metrics -> metric_values (Float value) + event_metric_breakdowns -> metric_value_breakdowns (reuse metric_rows.py UPSERT helpers); reuse core/adapters BaseAdapter + core/intervals.py + chunk runner + ScanJob lifecycle; reuse anomaly_detector + MetricAnomaly/MetricBreakdownAnomaly (scope_type/scope_ref already generalize) + full alerting path; reuse MonitoringDetailPage + charts + lib/metrics.ts.

NEW-COST areas: (a) aggregations beyond COUNT in all 3 adapters + measure/SQL validator (breaks count-only positional-row contract + identifier-allowlist security model); (b) a metric scope threaded through ~6 hardcoded scope chains (no central registry): anomaly_detector, detect.py, signals.py, dispatch.py, rule_matches_anomaly, get_active_signals; (c) the event_composition evaluator (bucket alignment + densify, divide-by-zero -> null, distinct-user denominator).

Subsumes tripl-oqse (Platform volume parity / ratio anomaly).

Build order: M1 -> {M2, M4}; M3 parallel; M2 -> {M5, M7}; M3 -> M5; M5 -> M6; {M4, M7} -> M8; {M6, M8} -> M9.
close_reason: Epic complete: user-defined Metrics catalog + monitoring shipped across 9 slices (.1 model+enums, .2 value storage, .3 adapter aggregations+validator, .4 catalog API, .5 collection task, .6 anomaly scope+alerting, .7 series read, .8 frontend, .9 integration tests+docs). Full backend suite 801 passed; frontend tsc/eslint/vitest clean. Delivered on branch feat/metrics-catalog (local).

title: Fix asyncio loop reuse in worker/search_reindex.py (Celery->async bridge)
description: reindex_main_branch_from_worker() (called from sync Celery tasks scan.py:213 and metrics/tasks.py:401) bridges to async via asyncio.run(_run()), and _run() uses the module-global pooled async engine (database.py). asyncpg binds connections to the loop that opened them; asyncio.run() makes a fresh loop each call. In a long-lived prefork worker, the 2nd+ reindex per process checks out a connection bound to an already-closed loop -> RuntimeError 'got Future attached to a different loop' / 'Event loop is closed'. The bare 'except Exception' swallows it, so search silently stops reindexing after the first scan/metrics run. Deterministic on 3.14 (asyncio.run always allocates a fresh loop; legacy implicit-loop fallbacks removed). Tests pass because the sqlite suite short-circuits at the postgresql dialect guard.
acceptance_criteria: Each invocation builds a throwaway NullPool async engine fully contained in its asyncio.run() loop and disposes it in finally (or routes through the sync engine). Regression test asserts a fresh engine is created+disposed per call. ruff+mypy green.
close_reason: Fixed: _run() builds a throwaway NullPool async engine per asyncio.run() loop and disposes it in finally; removed module-global async_session import; captured project.slug before the coroutine. Added test_search_reindex.py (2 sync regression tests). ruff+mypy green; tests pass under -W error::ResourceWarning.

Screen reader users cannot determine the button's purpose or current expansion state. - **Fix:** Add `aria-label` and `aria-expanded`: ```tsx <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={expanded ? 'Collapse job details' : 'Expand job details'} aria-expanded={expanded} onClick={onToggle} > <ChevronDown className={`size-3 transition-transform ${expanded ? 'rotate-180' : ''}`} aria-hidden="true" /> </Button> ``` - [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/settings/VariablesTab.tsx`:294-295 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Icon-only Edit and Delete variable buttons have no accessible name - `<Button size="icon">` wrapping `<Pencil>` and `<Trash2>` for each variable row have no `aria-label` or `title`. Screen reader users cannot identify the action or target. - **Fix:** Add `aria-label` including the variable name: ```tsx <Button aria-label={`Edit variable ${v.name}`} variant="ghost" size="icon" ...> <Pencil className="h-3 w-3" /> </Button> <Button aria-label={`Delete variable ${v.name}`} variant="ghost" size="icon" ...> <Trash2 className="h-3 w-3" /> </Button> ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/app-sidebar.tsx`:556-584 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Collapsed sidebar nav links use title-only accessible names - In CollapsedSidebar, each icon-only <Link> at lines 560-583 uses only title={item.label} with no aria-label. The title attribute is not reliably announced as an accessible name by VoiceOver on iOS or NVDA in Browse mode when the element is focused. The lucide icons inside are also not aria-hidden. This means icon-only navigation links may have no announced name, failing WCAG 4.1.2. - **Fix:** Replace title with aria-label on each Link: <Link ... aria-label={item.label}> and remove the title prop. Add aria-hidden="true" to <Icon className="h-[15px] w-[15px]" aria-hidden="true" />. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/app-sidebar.tsx`:540-545 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Collapsed sidebar Search button uses title-only accessible name - The Search <button> at line 539 in CollapsedSidebar uses only title="Search · ⌘K" with no aria-label. This relies on the title tooltip for its accessible name, which is not reliable across all screen reader/browser combinations, failing WCAG 4.1.2. - **Fix:** Replace title with aria-label: <button type="button" aria-label="Search or jump — ⌘K" ...> and add aria-hidden="true" to <Search className="h-3.5 w-3.5" aria-hidden="true" />. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/monitoring/release-regression-panel.tsx`:21-26 (WCAG 1.1.1) — Decorative Lucide icons in RegressionRow are not aria-hidden - The `Icon` variable (either `PackageX` or `TrendingDown`, line 21) is rendered at line 26 as a Lucide SVG alongside descriptive text (`item.scope_name`, version info). The SVG has no `aria-hidden="true"`, so screen readers will attempt to read it — Lucide icons render with no title element, producing unlabeled SVG noise (some screen readers announce the SVG element type). The icon is purely decorative here; the adjacent text already conveys the meaning. WCAG 1.1.1 requires decorative images to be hidden from assistive technology. - **Fix:** Add `aria-hidden="true"` to the icon: ```tsx <Icon aria-hidden="true" className="mt-0.5 h-4 w-4 shrink-0 text-destructive" /> ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/monitoring/top-movers-panel.tsx`:124-126 (WCAG 1.1.1) — Decorative Lucide icons in TopMoverRow are not aria-hidden - The `ChevronIcon` (ChevronDown/ChevronRight, line 125) and `Icon` (ArrowUp/ArrowDown, line 124) in `TopMoverRow` are rendered without `aria-hidden="true"`. The expand/collapse state is already communicated via `aria-expanded` on the parent button (line 132), and the direction (spike vs. drop) is conveyed by the adjacent text label. The decorative SVG icons therefore produce redundant or uninformative announcements for screen reader users. WCAG 1.1.1 requires decorative images to have a null/hidden text alternative. - **Fix:** Add `aria-hidden="true"` to both icon elements: ```tsx <ChevronIcon aria-hidden="true" className="h-3.5 w-3.5 shrink-0 text-muted-foreground" /> ... <Icon aria-hidden="true" className="h-3 w-3" /> ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/monitoring/top-movers-panel.tsx`:233-258 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Recharts breakdown timeline chart has no accessible label - The `BreakdownDrilldown` component renders a `<ResponsiveContainer>` / `<ComposedChart>` (line 235) that is a purely visual timeline chart. Recharts renders into an SVG with no `role="img"`, no `aria-label`, and no `<title>` element. A screen reader user who navigates to this expanded section encounters an unlabeled graphic conveying no information. WCAG 4.1.2 requires non-text content to have a text alternative. - **Fix:** Wrap the ResponsiveContainer in a `<div role="img" aria-label="...">` with a meaningful label, or add a `<title>` element inside the SVG via Recharts' `customized` prop: ```tsx <div role="img" aria-label={`Timeline for ${breakdownColumn}=${breakdownValue}`} className="h-[120px] w-full" > <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height="100%"> <ComposedChart ...> ... </ComposedChart> </ResponsiveContainer> </div> ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/settings/SettingsLayout.tsx`:129-155 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Active nav item has no aria-current="page" - The sidebar navigation renders nav item `<button>` elements and highlights the active route by visual styling only (background/color tokens, lines 139-141). There is no `aria-current` attribute on the active item, so screen reader users cannot identify which settings section is currently open. WCAG 4.1.2 requires the state of UI components to be programmatically determinable. - **Fix:** Add `aria-current="page"` (or `aria-current="true"`) to the active button: ```tsx <button key={item.id} type="button" aria-current={active ? 'page' : undefined} onClick={() => onNavigate(item.path)} ... > ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/theme-toggle.tsx`:15-28 (WCAG 4.1.2) — ThemeToggle button missing type and uses title-only accessible name - The <button> at line 15 has no type attribute (defaults to type="submit" inside a form context, which could cause unintended form submissions) and uses only title={`Theme: ${theme}`} with no aria-label. The icon-only nature and title-only name make this inaccessible to screen readers in some AT configurations, violating WCAG 4.1.2. - **Fix:** Add type="button" and aria-label: <button type="button" aria-label={`Switch theme — current: ${theme}`} ...>. Add aria-hidden="true" to each icon (Sun, Moon, Monitor) since the name is on the button. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/top-bar.tsx`:135-142 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Notifications button relies only on title and does not expose badge count to AT - The notifications <button> at line 137 in NotificationsMenu uses only title="Notifications" with no aria-label. The numeric badge span at line 149 showing the count (e.g. '3') has no accessible context and will be read without meaning. Screen readers miss the full notification count in the button's name, violating WCAG 4.1.2. - **Fix:** Use a dynamic aria-label: aria-label={badgeCount > 0 ? `Notifications — ${badgeCount} active` : 'Notifications'}. Remove the title prop. Add aria-hidden="true" to the Bell icon and to the badge span (count is expressed in the label). - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/top-bar.tsx`:90-105 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Activity panel toggle button has no accessible name and missing aria-pressed - The 'Now' toggle button at line 90 uses only title="Toggle activity panel" with no aria-label. Additionally, it acts as a toggle (pressed/unpressed state expressed via background/border styling only) but has no aria-pressed attribute, so screen readers cannot convey its current state. This fails WCAG 4.1.2. - **Fix:** Add aria-label="Toggle activity panel" and aria-pressed={activityOpen} to the button. Remove the title prop. Example: <button type="button" aria-label="Toggle activity panel" aria-pressed={activityOpen} ...>. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/tweaks-panel.tsx`:48-63 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Tweaks trigger button accessible name relies only on title attribute - The floating trigger button at line 48 uses title="Tweaks" as its only accessible name. The title attribute is not reliably announced by all screen readers (particularly on mobile AT and VoiceOver in some modes) and is not a sufficient accessible name per WCAG 4.1.2. The Sliders icon inside has no aria-hidden. - **Fix:** Replace title with aria-label: <button type="button" aria-label="Open tweaks panel" ...> and add aria-hidden="true" to <Sliders className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/AuthPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 4.1.2) — Auth mode toggle buttons have no selected-state communicated to AT - The two-button toggle at lines 102–126 ("Existing Account" / "Create Account") uses plain `<button>` elements styled to indicate the active mode visually, but carries no `aria-pressed` or `role="tab"` to communicate which mode is currently selected to screen reader users. - **Fix:** Add `aria-pressed` to each button: ```tsx <button type="button" aria-pressed={mode === 'login'} onClick={() => setMode('login')} ... > Existing Account </button> <button type="button" aria-pressed={mode === 'register'} onClick={() => setMode('register')} ... > Create Account </button> ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/ReconciliationPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 4.1.2) — Shadow event tab filter buttons have no selected-state ARIA attribute - The three filter buttons ("new", "accepted", "dismissed") at lines 212–227 visually indicate the active tab via background color but expose no `aria-pressed` or `aria-selected` to AT. Screen reader users cannot determine which filter is currently active. - **Fix:** Add `aria-pressed` to each button: ```tsx <button key={tab} type="button" aria-pressed={shadowStatus === tab} onClick={() => setShadowStatus(tab)} ... > {tab} </button> ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/settings-area/ProjectGeneralSection.tsx`:214-231 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Accent color picker buttons have non-descriptive aria-labels using raw oklch values - Each color swatch `<button aria-label={`Accent ${c}`}>` (line 221) exposes raw oklch strings like `"Accent oklch(0.72 0.14 192)"` as the accessible name. This is meaningless to screen reader users who cannot map a color function to a perceptual color. - **Fix:** Define human-readable color names alongside the ACCENT_COLORS array (e.g., `{ value: 'oklch(0.72 0.14 192)', label: 'Teal' }`) and use the label in `aria-label`: `aria-label={`Accent color: ${colorName}${accent === c ? ', selected' : ''}`}`. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/settings/MetaFieldsTab.tsx`:171, 250 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Enum option remove buttons use a bare × character as their only label - The inline `<button>×</button>` rendered for each enum chip (both create and edit dialogs) has only a raw multiplication sign as text content. This is not an understandable accessible name; screen readers typically announce it as "times" or "multiplication sign" with no indication of which option will be removed. - **Fix:** Use a visually-hidden text label or `aria-label`: ```tsx <button type="button" aria-label={`Remove option ${opt}`} onClick={() => setEnumOptions(enumOptions.filter(o => o !== opt))} className="hover:text-destructive" > <span aria-hidden="true">×</span> </button> ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/settings/scans/EventGroupRulesEditor.tsx`:96-105 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Icon-only 'Remove group rule' button uses title instead of aria-label - The `<Button size="icon">` at line 96 contains only `<Trash2 className="h-4 w-4" />` with no visible text. It relies on `title="Remove group rule"` (line 101) for its accessible name. `title` is not reliably exposed as an accessible name on interactive elements by all screen readers and is invisible to touch/voice users. The same pattern applies to the 'Remove condition' button at lines 134–146. - **Fix:** Replace `title` with `aria-label` on both icon buttons: ```tsx <Button type="button" variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={`Remove group rule "${rule.name}"`} className="self-end text-muted-foreground hover:text-destructive" onClick={() => onChange(rules.filter((_, index) => index !== ruleIndex))} > <Trash2 className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden /> </Button> ``` And for the condition button: ```tsx <Button ... aria-label="Remove condition"> <Trash2 className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden /> </Button> ``` - [ ] **[LOW]** `components/activity-panel.tsx`:69-79 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Refresh activity button accessible name relies only on title attribute - The refresh <button> at line 69 uses only title="Refresh activity" with no aria-label. The RefreshCw icon is not aria-hidden. Title-only accessible names are unreliable on touch/mobile screen readers. - **Fix:** Add aria-label="Refresh activity" to the button and aria-hidden="true" to <RefreshCw className="h-[13px] w-[13px]" aria-hidden="true" />. - [ ] **[LOW]** `components/primitives/dot.tsx`:21-28 (WCAG 1.4.1) — Dot status indicator is not aria-hidden and conveys no accessible state - The `Dot` component renders a `<span>` that communicates status/tone (success, warning, danger, etc.) and optionally a pulse animation purely through background color. It has no `aria-hidden="true"` and no text alternative. When used as a standalone status indicator (e.g. in `MiniStat`), color-blind users and screen reader users receive no state information. WCAG 1.4.1 prohibits color as the sole means of conveying information. - **Fix:** When `Dot` conveys meaningful status, include a visually hidden label. For decorative use (alongside text already describing state), add `aria-hidden="true"`: ```tsx // Decorative alongside text: <span aria-hidden="true" className={cn('inline-block rounded-full shrink-0', ...)} style={...} /> // Meaningful standalone: <span className={cn(...)} style={...} role="img" aria-label={`${tone} status`} /> ``` - [ ] **[LOW]** `components/top-bar.tsx`:75-86 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Command palette button accessible name relies only on title attribute - The 'Command palette' button at line 75 uses only title="Command palette" with no aria-label. The Search icon inside is not aria-hidden. Title-only names are unreliable across assistive technologies. The icon, being decorative beside the Kbd shortcut display, should also be aria-hidden to avoid double-announcement. - **Fix:** Add aria-label="Command palette" to the button and aria-hidden="true" to <Search className="h-[13px] w-[13px]" aria-hidden="true" />. - [ ] **[LOW]** `pages/settings/scans/ScanConfigRow.tsx`:105 (WCAG 1.3.1) — Decorative '›' character in last table cell has no aria-hidden - The last `<td>` at line 105 renders a bare `›` glyph as a visual chevron indicator. Screen readers will read this as 'right-pointing angle quotation mark' or similar, adding noise without meaning. - **Fix:** Add `aria-hidden="true"` to the cell or its content: ```tsx <td className="w-10 px-3.5 py-2.5 align-middle text-[var(--fg-faint)]" aria-hidden="true">›</td> ``` ### Acceptance - All checklist items addressed in code - `pnpm lint` passes (jsx-a11y rules) and relevant `pnpm test` axe assertions green
close_reason: Fixed via audit+remediation workflow; verified by tsc/lint/test/build gates.

title: Frontend accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) remediation
description:
## Frontend accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) remediation

Systematic accessibility hardening of the React 19 + Radix UI + shadcn/ui frontend.

### How this was found
Parallel WCAG 2.2 AA audit across all 154 component files (9 file groups), each finding independently re-verified by an adversarial reviewer to remove false positives. Result: **133 raw -> 9 refuted -> 124 confirmed findings** across 62 files.

### Severity breakdown
- CRITICAL: 10 (blocks a core task for assistive-tech users)
- HIGH: 66 (significant barrier)
- MEDIUM: 40 (degraded experience)
- LOW: 8 (polish)

### Theme breakdown
- name-role-value (48): icon-only buttons / dialogs / toggles with no accessible name
- form-label (39): inputs/selects/labels not programmatically associated; missing aria-invalid/aria-describedby
- live-region (15): async status/errors/results updating silently
- semantic-html (9) + keyboard-nav (3) + target-size (2): non-semantic interactive elements, click-only handlers, tiny hit targets
- aria-misuse (8): incorrect/contradictory ARIA

### Approach
Fix-everything mandate (all severities, including the vendored components/ui/* shadcn primitives). Plus systemic prevention: add eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y (flat config, zero-warning policy) and vitest-axe so regressions fail CI going forward.

### Acceptance (epic done when)
- All child tasks closed
- pnpm lint passes with jsx-a11y rules enabled and --max-warnings 0
- pnpm test green (incl. new axe smoke assertions)
- pnpm build (full type check) green
close_reason: All 8 children complete. 124 WCAG 2.2 AA findings remediated across 76 files + guardrails. Gates: tsc 0, lint 0, test 167/167, build OK.

title: Move search reindex out of the write request transaction (double-commit + latency)
description:
HIGH — confirmed pattern. `event_service.create_event` commits at line 268 then synchronously calls `reindex_project_branch(...)` (line 271), which issues its own DELETE/flush/commit on the SAME session (search_service.py:170). Repeats across `update_event`, `delete_event`, `bulk_create_events`, `bulk_update_events`, `bulk_delete_events`. Two problems: (1) a second commit after the primary commit — if reindex raises, the request-scoped rollback in `database.get_session` can leave primary data and the search index inconsistent; (2) the full per-branch index rebuild runs inline, holding the HTTP response open for a potentially multi-second operation.

Fix: dispatch the reindex as a Celery task (the `_queue_embedding_refresh` pattern already exists and embeddings already refresh out-of-band → index is eventually consistent anyway). Removes both the double-commit window and the latency. Add a test asserting the mutation commits independently of reindex success.
close_reason: Done: atomic same-transaction reindex (no Celery — tests not eager). Extracted no-commit _reindex_branch_documents; all 6 mutation paths reindex before a single commit; embedding refresh fires post-commit. Atomicity test added. Green.

title: Add editor scope gate to POST /ai/ask; audit scope deps across mutating/LLM routes
description:
HIGH — confirmed. `api/v1/ai.py:67 ask_plan` has NO user dependency, unlike its siblings `describe_event`/`describe_event_type` which both inject `_current_user: EditorUserDep`. The route IS still authenticated (the whole v1 router mounts `Depends(get_current_user)` in router.py), but any authenticated principal — including a read-scoped API key or viewer role — can invoke the LLM and run a full semantic search over plan data (quota + minor data-access concern).

Fix: add `_current_user: EditorUserDep` to `ask_plan` to match siblings. While here, grep all `@router.post/put/patch/delete` handlers and confirm each mutating or LLM-invoking route declares the intended scope dep (EditorUserDep/OwnerUserDep/WriteUserDep) — add a test asserting a read-scoped key gets 403 on `/ai/ask`.
notes: CLOSED as invalid (false positive) after code verification on 2026-06-21. ask_plan is READ-ONLY (ai_service.py:183 — wraps search_service.search_project + LLM summarization, no DB mutation). GET /search (search.py:14) requires only authentication, NOT EditorUserDep — so any authenticated user (incl. viewer) already sees this data. An editor gate on /ask would be STRICTER than the search it summarizes — wrong direction. The editor gate on sibling describe_event/describe_event_type is fine (authoring feature). Residual (LLM quota for read users) is a rate-limit concern, not access control; rate-limit middleware already exists.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add SSRF guards on owner-configurable URLs and DB hosts (ai_base_url, data source host)
description:
HIGH — confirmed pattern. Two owner-settable network targets reach the backend with no private/internal-address validation, while the same `reject_private_host` / `_validate_https_url` helpers already exist in `alerting_validation.py` and are wired for alert channels:

1. `AiSettingsUpdate.ai_base_url` (schemas/app_settings.py:129) is free-form `str | None`. `llm_service` POSTs to it WITH the API key in the Authorization header — an owner can point it at `http://169.254.169.254/...` (cloud metadata) or internal services.
2. `DataSourceCreate.host` / `DataSourceUpdate.host` (schemas/data_source.py:12) accept any string; `POST /data-sources/{id}/test` then connects via the worker adapter to that host (RFC1918 / metadata reachable).

Fix: add `@field_validator` on `ai_base_url` → `_validate_https_url(..., block_private_hosts=True)`; add `@field_validator("host")` on the data-source schemas → `reject_private_host(...)`; re-check host in `datasource_service._run_adapter_test` as a DNS-rebinding defense (mirror the alert send-time re-validation). Note: treat as deployment-policy dependent if single-trusted-owner model, but the guard is cheap.
notes: SCOPE DECISION (user, 2026-06-21): FORMAT-ONLY validation, NO IP blocking. Rationale: data-source hosts are normally private DBs (10.x/VPC) and ai_base_url is often localhost (local LLM) — reject_private_host would break legit self-hosted deployments; single-operator trust model makes RFC1918 SSRF low-risk. Implement: (1) ai_base_url — validate well-formed http(s) URL with non-empty host (NOT _validate_https_url which forces https + can block private); allow http for local LLMs. (2) data_source host — validate non-empty/sane hostname-or-IP format only. Do NOT call reject_private_host anywhere. To be done as a follow-up after workflow wlo3pb72u lands (files schemas/app_settings.py, schemas/data_source.py, services/datasource_service.py are disjoint from the running lanes but editing during the workflow verify phase would collide).
close_reason: Done: format-only validators (no IP blocking, per user) on DataSource host + AiSettingsUpdate.ai_base_url; allows private DBs/localhost LLMs, rejects malformed. 19 tests. Green.

title: Redact alerting destination secrets from audit log
description:
HIGH — confirmed. `api/v1/alerting.py:47,84` call `audit_service.record(payload=data.model_dump())` for create/update destination. `AlertDestinationCreate` (schemas/alerting.py:159) carries secret fields `webhook_url`, `bot_token`, `target_url`, `webhook_header_value`, `jira_api_token`, `linear_api_key`. `audit_service._redact` (audit_service.py:29) matches keys EXACTLY against `_REDACTED_KEYS = {password, password_encrypted, password_hash, secret, token, credentials}` — none of those alerting field names match, so the secrets land in `audit_log.payload` in cleartext, readable via `GET .../audit`.

Fix: add the six alerting key names to `_REDACTED_KEYS`, OR pass `data.model_dump(exclude={...secrets...})` at both alerting.py call sites. Prefer widening `_REDACTED_KEYS` (defense in depth) and add a regression test that creates a Slack/webhook/Jira/Linear destination and asserts the audit payload shows `***`.
close_reason: Done: widened audit_service._REDACTED_KEYS to cover 6 alerting destination secret keys + from_attributes on Alert*Response; test_audit unit test. Green.

title: FastAPI review remediation: security, async/data-access, API hygiene
description:
Remediation epic from a focused FastAPI review (4 parallel fastapi-reviewer passes: app-core, routers/schemas, async/data-access, security) of `backend/src/tripl` on 2026-06-21.

## Scope reviewed
- App factory / lifespan / middleware / CORS / OpenAPI (main.py, config.py, deps.py, database.py, middleware/*)
- 26 v1 routers + all Pydantic schemas
- Service layer async correctness, DB sessions, external HTTP/LLM/SSRF
- AuthN/AuthZ, API keys, crypto/secrets, rate limiting, data-source connections

## Verified false positives (NOT filed)
- "CRITICAL: `except A, B:` Python-2 syntax breaks auth/llm/worker modules" — FALSE. Verified at runtime on Python 3.14.6: parenthesis-free multi-exception `except` (PEP 758) parses AND catches both types correctly; `requires-python = ">=3.14"`. ruff + full pytest pass.
- "HIGH: data-source `password` leaks into audit log" — OVERSTATED. The key `password` IS in `_REDACTED_KEYS` (exact match) and is redacted to `***`. (The alerting-secrets leak below is the real one — different key names.)

Child tasks carry the confirmed findings, grouped by theme and severity. Verify each fix with `uv run pytest` + `uv run mypy` + `uv run ruff check`.
notes: Verified false positive #3: 'POST /ai/ask missing editor gate' (was lyo9.3) — CLOSED invalid. ask_plan is read-only and only exposes what GET /search (auth-only, no editor) already gives any authenticated user; an editor gate would be stricter than the underlying search. Confirmed product intent: viewers can ask the LLM.
close_reason: FastAPI review remediation complete. 10 substantive fixes shipped & verified (ruff+mypy clean, 540+ pytest passing, 2 adversarial review passes clean); 2 findings correctly resolved as false-positive/won't-do (lyo9.3 editor gate, lyo9.12 item 1 lazy=raise). All children terminal.

title: P1 — Make page widths consistent (Scans + others not full-width)
description:
## P1 — Make page widths consistent (Scans + others not using full width)

**Defect (reported):** «страница сканов не на всю ширину, может и другие» — the Scans page sits in
a narrow column with empty space on the right on wide monitors, while sibling pages fill the
viewport. Suspected to affect other pages too.

### Current behavior / root cause
The app shell `Layout.tsx` (lines 144-160) gives the content area full width by design — the scroll
container + padding wrapper set **no** max-width. Width caps come from the page itself. Most surfaces
honor full width (Overview, Monitors, Alerting, Events, and all settings LIST tabs). But four
surfaces opt into a hardcoded cap as **duplicated literal classes** — accidental redesign drift, not
a deliberate per-page decision (the values even disagree: 1040 vs 1100):

| File | Line | Offending class |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend/src/pages/settings/ScansTab.tsx` | 109 | `max-w-[1040px]` (Scans **list** — primary report) |
| `frontend/src/pages/settings/ScanConfigDetailView.tsx` | 72 | `max-w-[1040px]` (single-scan **detail**) |
| `frontend/src/pages/settings/EventTypeDetailView.tsx` | 158 | `max-w-[1040px]` (event-type detail) |
| `frontend/src/pages/ReconciliationPage.tsx` | 138 | `max-w-[1100px]` (Reconciliation) |

Full-width reference pattern: `OverviewPage.tsx:102` (`min-w-0 space-y-8 pb-12`),
`MonitorsPage.tsx:42`, `EventsPage.tsx:259`, `EventTypesTab.tsx:102`, plus MetaFields/Relations/
Variables/Monitoring/Audit/History/Branches (all `space-y-4`/`flex-col gap`, no cap).

### Proposed fix (className-only, **zero deps**)

title: [EPIC] Post-redesign polish: page width, scan replay, events table, SQL editor, bulk-bar
description:
## Post-redesign polish — visual/interaction defects after the Data-first redesign

Follow-up to the now-closed redesign epic **tripl-f7q6** ("Data-first redesign: align
frontend to new Claude Design mockups"). After that landed, manual review surfaced five
visual/interaction defects that the surface-by-surface port missed. This epic closes them.

### The five defects (one child task each)
1. **P1 — Page width inconsistency.** Scans list + Scan detail (and, for consistency,
   event-type detail + Reconciliation) opt into a hardcoded `max-w-[1040px]`/`max-w-[1100px]`
   cap while their sibling pages are full-width → they look accidentally narrow on wide monitors.
2. **P2 — Scan Replay button "disappeared".** The trigger still exists, but after the
   modal→inline refactor (tripl-f7q6.15) the inline panel renders at the top of the
   Configuration tab while its button sits in the bottom Danger zone, so clicking it opens the
   panel off-screen — the feature appears gone in the real browser.
3. **P3 — Inline Events table right-edge + native controls.** Scrollbar detached from the
   table frame, content bleeds past the right edge, and the inline status editor is a raw
   native `<select>` with native `title` tooltips ("ugly popup with a name").
4. **P4 — SQL editor for scans.** The "Base query" field is a plain `<textarea>`; the user
   wants syntax highlighting + a Format action. (Enhancement beyond the mockup; only task that
   needs new dependencies.)
5. **P5 — Events bulk-action bar.** Actions look disabled (muted ghost/placeholder contrast on
   the dark bar) and "Assign owner…" wraps to two lines in a fixed `w-32` Select trigger.

### Why these cluster (cross-cutting)
- **`frontend/src/pages/EventsPage.tsx`** hosts BOTH P3 (table frame) and P5 (bulk bar), and
  its embedded variant is what **EventTypeDetailView.tsx** renders — the same file P1 un-caps.
- **`EventTypeDetailView.tsx`** is touched by P1 (remove width cap, line 158) and P3 (embedded
  `<EventsPage lockType embedded />`, line 129) — independent edits, but **do P1 first** so P3's
  framed table is verified at full width.
- **`.tripl-table-wrap`** (index.css:148-155) is **single-use** (only EventsTable.tsx:166) →
  de-risks P3's "CSS affects every table" worry. Prefer framing via a wrapper div in EventsPage
  so the footer is enclosed too.
- **shadcn Select trigger** (`components/ui/select.tsx:19`, `data-[placeholder]:text-muted-foreground`
  + transparent bg) is the shared root of the "greyed" look in BOTH P3 and P5. P3 *adopts* the
  primitive; P5 *overrides* its muted defaults via className. **Neither edits select.tsx** (that
  is tripl-1p25's scope). Coordinate the compact-trigger className convention so row editor and
  bulk bar read consistently.
- **EventStatus primitives** (`lib/eventStatus.ts` TONE/DOT_TONE/LABELS + Chip + Dot) reused by
  P3's new selector and the read-only EventRow chip.
- **Scans area**: P2 edits ScanConfigForm.tsx; P4 edits ScanFormSections.tsx (the
  SourceQuerySection ScanConfigForm renders) — adjacent, no file collision. Both prove the single
  shared SourceQuerySection swap covers create + edit.

### Recommended execution order
**P1 → P5 → P2 → P3 → P4.** P1 first (sets width context for P3); P5 next (settles the Select
convention P3 mirrors); P2 grouped with scans-area QA; P3 after P1+P5 (needs real-browser
interaction QA for the portal'd Select inside the hover overlay); P4 last and gated on dependency
sign-off.

### Dependency footprint
- P1, P2, P3, P5 add **zero** new deps (radix select/tooltip, lucide, react-query, cva,
  tailwind-merge all present).
- **P4 is the only task adding deps** (CodeMirror stack + sql-formatter, ~45–60KB gzip). Must use
  **pnpm add** (lockfile policy) and is gated on explicit bundle-budget sign-off.

### Constraints (inherited from tripl-f7q6)
- Stack: React 19 + TS + Vite + Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui. Reuse existing primitives
  (chip, dot, sparkline, mini-stat, sensitivity-chip) and `ui/` components.
- **pnpm only** (never npm/yarn). Quality gates: `pnpm lint` (zero warnings), `pnpm test`,
  `pnpm build` (full type check). Do not regress existing tests.
- Keep authoring and review in separate passes.
- Mockups live (gitignored) under `design/tripl/`; where mockup and real API/types disagree, the
  **real types win**.

> Investigated read-only by a 6-agent workflow (per-defect file/line evidence captured in each
> child task). Implementation NOT started — these are specs.

title: Foundation: design tokens, primitives & status lifecycle alignment
description:
## Foundation: design tokens, shared primitives & status lifecycle alignment

Shared groundwork the other 8 surface tasks build on. Most of this already exists in the repo
(`index.css`, `components/primitives/`, `components/ui/`) — this task is to **audit and align**
to the mockup, not rebuild.

### Mockup reference
- `design/tripl/project/styles.css` (tokens, form controls, toggle, nav item)
- `design/tripl/project/primitives.jsx` (`Icon`, `Sparkline`, `Dot`, `Chip`, `Btn`)
- `design/tripl/project/data.jsx` lines 40–48 (`STATUS_LABELS`, `STATUS_TONE`)

### Real files
- `frontend/src/index.css`
- `frontend/src/components/primitives/{chip,dot,sparkline,mini-stat,kbd,sensitivity-chip}.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/ui/{button,badge,select,switch,input,textarea}.tsx`

### Details to verify / align
- **Tokens**: radius 8/6/12; surfaces (`--bg`,`--bg-elevated`,`--bg-sunken`,`--surface`,
  `--surface-hover`,`--surface-active`); fg `--fg/--fg-muted/--fg-subtle/--fg-faint`;
  borders `--border/-strong/-subtle`; semantic `success/warning/danger/info` + `-soft`;
  shadows sm/md/lg. Density classes set `--row-h` to 28/36/44; `--header-h` 44.
- **Decision**: mockup defaults density to **compact**; repo default is **cozy**. Decide
  whether to switch the default (mockup chose compact for 2k+ row scale). Flag, don't assume.
- **Chip**: sizes xs/sm/md (h 18/20/24, fs 10.5/11/12); tones neutral/accent/success/warning/
  danger/info; variants soft/outline; optional leading icon. Confirm parity.
- **Btn**: variants primary/secondary/ghost/outline/danger; sizes xs/sm/md (h 22/28/32);
  icon-only square at sm (28×28); `active` state for toggles.
- **Sparkline**: variants line / line-only (stroke) / bar; gradient area fill; `anomalyIdx`
  marker (danger dot/bar); width/height props.
- **Dot**: tones + `pulse` animation (1.8s); sizes.
- **Status lifecycle** (single source of truth): `draft→in_review→ready_for_dev→implemented→
  live→deprecated→archived` with tones draft=neutral, in_review=warning, ready_for_dev=info,
  implemented=success, live=success, deprecated=warning, archived=neutral. Reconcile with the
  real status enum in `types/`; expose shared `STATUS_LABELS`/`STATUS_TONE` helpers.
- **Sensitivity**: none/pii/phi/financial/secret with the mockup `SENS_STYLE` colors; reuse

### Acceptance
- Token + primitive parity checklist completed; any gaps closed or filed as follow-ups.
- Shared status/sensitivity helpers in one place, used by events/types tasks.
- `pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build` green. No visual regression on existing pages.

title: Data-first redesign: align frontend to new Claude Design mockups
description:
## Data-first redesign — align frontend to the new Claude Design mockups

A new design handoff bundle (Claude Design, "Linear meets Stripe for tracking plans")
reworks the major Tripl surfaces. This epic tracks bringing the real `frontend/` in line
with those mockups, surface by surface, with attention to visual detail.

### Where the design lives
- Local, gitignored: `design/tripl/` (see `design/tripl/AGENTS.md` for the full file map).
- Read `design/tripl/chats/chat1.md` + `chat2.md` for intent, then `project/Tripl.html` + imports.
- Mockup data was reverse-engineered from the repo; **where mockup and real types disagree,
  the real API/types win** (e.g. `ScanConfig`, `eventTypes.ts`, the 7-state lifecycle).

### Design language (already mostly in `index.css` + `components/{primitives,ui}`)
- Type: Inter (UI) + JetBrains Mono (numbers/ids/event names). Tabular nums on metrics.
- Accent: teal `oklch(0.72 0.14 192)` default, 5 accents, dark default + light toggle.
- Density: compact 28 / cozy 36 / comfy 44px rows; header 44px.
- Tone scale: success/warning/danger/info with `-soft` variants; 4-tier fg hierarchy.
- Signals are inline (z-score chips, sparklines, pulse dots) — never tooltip-gated.

### Reworked surfaces (one task each)
1. Sidebar / app shell / navigation
2. Events list / table
3. Single event page + edit
4. Event types screen + type settings
5. Scans: list + single scan + edit/create
6. Plan branches
7. Reconciliation
8. Settings (full-takeover area)

Plus: a shared foundation task (tokens/primitives/lifecycle alignment) and a final visual
verification pass.

### Constraints
- Stack: React + TS + Vite + Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui. Reuse existing primitives
  (`chip`, `dot`, `sparkline`, `mini-stat`, `sensitivity-chip`) and `ui/` components.
- `pnpm` only (never npm/yarn). Quality gates: `pnpm lint` (zero warnings), `pnpm test`,
  `pnpm build` (full type check).
- Keep authoring and review in separate passes. Do not regress existing tests.
close_reason: All redesign surfaces ported to the Claude Design mockups; final children .11 (inline scoped Events table in type-detail) and .33 (Instance settings sub-card restyle) complete. Frontend gates green: tsc -b, eslint zero-warnings, 156 tests.

Add a data cleanup step that merges duplicate Variable rows and their VariableValue contexts before the enum column rewrite rebuilds unique indexes.
close_reason: Added production data cleanup to merge duplicate variables and variable value contexts before enum table rewrites rebuild unique indexes.

title: Release-regression analyzer + ReleaseRegression model
description: New analyzer: for each event (and event_type) compare latest version vs previous version using T4's normalization and flag 'event missing in new release' and 'volume regressed in new release'. New ReleaseRegression model to store signals (missing-event is not a z-score anomaly, so it needs its own representation). Integrate into the metrics recalculation flow and populate result_summary counters.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic-series unit tests for missing/regressed/healthy cases; signals persisted & re-derived idempotently; result_summary reports counts; analyzer skipped entirely when column unset. ACCEPTANCE (cross-cutting): feature is fully inert when scan_config.app_version_column IS NULL — no extra warehouse queries, no version series, no regression signals, no alerts, no UI. Existing scans (incl. web with no app version) behave exactly as before.
close_reason: Added ReleaseRegression model + migration c2d3e4f5a6b7; pure analyzer worker/analyzers/release_regression.py implementing the decision-doc model (maturity gate on total-traffic share, activation-anchored overlap window, composition-share normalization, missing/volume_drop); recalc worker/tasks/metrics/regression.py wired into collect_metrics + result_summary[release_regressions_detected]; reuses sigma_threshold. Tests: 7 unit (analyzer) + 2 recalc (missing/idempotent, inert); full metrics suite 35 passed; ruff/mypy/alembic-graph clean. Inert when app_version_column unset.

title: DECISION: cross-version normalization model for regression comparison
description: Define how to compare a new release against the previous one given adoption skew (a fresh release has few users, so raw counts are not comparable). Decide the normalization (e.g. per-version share of that version's total events, or rate vs the version's project-total, and the adoption/minimum-volume gate before a regression can fire). Output: a written spec the analyzer (T5) implements.
acceptance_criteria: Decision doc records the normalization formula, the adoption gate, and the 'missing event' vs 'volume drop' criteria; reviewed before T5 starts.
notes: Decision recorded in internal/decisions/app-version-regression-model.md (kept out of the public docs/ set; beads task IDs stripped from the doc per review).
close_reason: Decision doc written at internal/decisions/app-version-regression-model.md: share-of-total maturity/active gate (excludes dev/tester build week), activation-anchored overlap window, composition-share normalization (expected vs observed), missing vs volume_drop classification, reuse of sigma_threshold/min_expected_count. Kept internal; beads jargon removed.

title: Collect per-version metric series with latest-N-release retention
description: When app_version_column is set, collect per-version series into EventMetricBreakdown (breakdown_column = app_version column). Replace the generic top-N-by-volume value selection with semver-aware retention: keep the latest N releases (app_version_keep_releases), group older releases into the 'other' bucket. Reuse the existing breakdown collection path; do not collect when column unset.
acceptance_criteria: Per-version rows stored & keyed correctly; retention keeps latest N by semver, not by volume; older releases collapse to is_other. ACCEPTANCE (cross-cutting): feature is fully inert when scan_config.app_version_column IS NULL — no extra warehouse queries, no version series, no regression signals, no alerts, no UI. Existing scans (incl. web with no app version) behave exactly as before.
close_reason: Added _collect_app_version_breakdown_rows in metric_rows.py: separate breakdown query with values_limit=None, SemVer-aware latest-N retention (app_version_keep_releases, default 10) via semver.order_versions, older releases folded into is_other "Other". Wired into process_chunk (chunk_processing.py) by merging version rows into breakdown_event/type_rows so delete/upsert/stats handle them uniformly. Inert (no warehouse query) when app_version_column is NULL. Test test_collect_metrics_retains_latest_app_versions_by_semver; 33 passed; ruff/mypy clean.

title: Semver utility (parse / compare / order) + unit tests
description: Backend utility to parse version strings into comparable keys, compare and order them (2.10.0 > 2.9.0), identify latest / previous release, with graceful lexical fallback for non-semver strings. Standalone, reusable by collection, retention and the regression analyzer.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover semver ordering, pre-release/build suffixes, mixed/invalid strings (deterministic fallback), latest/previous selection.
close_reason: Added standalone SemVer utility with parse/compare/order/latest-previous helpers and focused unit coverage for numeric ordering, prerelease/build precedence, invalid lexical fallback, and latest/previous selection. Tests: pytest src/tripl/tests/test_semver.py; ruff check semver/test_semver; mypy src/tripl/semver.py.

Reserve app_version_column like time_column/event_type_column (extend check_scalar_columns_unreserved so it cannot also be a metric_breakdown/distribution_drift field). Alembic migration following backend/alembic/versions/1b2c3d4e5f60_add_event_metric_breakdown_columns.py as template; chain after current head; add to test_alembic_revisions. Update frontend ScanConfig TS type + scans api client shape.
acceptance_criteria: Fields nullable, default NULL/inert. Migration up/down + revision-graph test pass. Validation rejects using app_version_column as breakdown/drift. ACCEPTANCE (cross-cutting): feature is fully inert when scan_config.app_version_column IS NULL — no extra warehouse queries, no version series, no regression signals, no alerts, no UI. Existing scans (incl. web with no app version) behave exactly as before.
close_reason: Added nullable app_version_column (String 255) + app_version_keep_releases (Integer) to ScanConfig; Create/Update/Response schemas; check_scalar_columns_unreserved now reserves app_version_column (rejects using it as breakdown/drift) incl. PATCH path; migration b1c2d3e4f5a6 (single head, up/down); frontend ScanConfig type + scans api client. Tests: 26 passed; ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc clean. Inert when column NULL.

title: App-version observation in scans
description: Optional app-version column on a scan config enables per-version metric observation: collect per-version series (semver-ordered, retain latest N releases), detect release regressions (event disappeared / volume dropped in the newest version vs the previous one), surface them in alerts and a dedicated monitoring view. Level C scope (full): semver parsing + latest-N retention, version adoption, latest-version filters, dedicated alert-rule type. Version column is OPTIONAL: ACCEPTANCE (cross-cutting): feature is fully inert when scan_config.app_version_column IS NULL — no extra warehouse queries, no version series, no regression signals, no alerts, no UI. Existing scans (incl. web with no app version) behave exactly as before.

title: Audit role permissions
description: Review RBAC and role enforcement for destructive and sensitive project changes, identify gaps, then implement focused fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Role-sensitive API operations are audited; missing enforcement is fixed; targeted tests cover corrected behavior.
close_reason: Implemented RBAC audit fixes: owner-only project deletion, owner-only data source management, API-key limits for owner-only routes, write-key role guard, UI controls aligned, and targeted tests added.

title: Preserve variable links on manual event edits; allow full event editing from event detail page
description: Manual event PATCH wiped all VariableValue rows (scan-observed variable contexts) whenever field_values were sent, because update_event deleted them alongside EventFieldValue. VariableValue is keyed by field_definition_id and upserted by scans, so manual edits must not touch it. Also: event detail page (MonitoringDetailPage) was read-only; added Edit button opening the full EventForm sheet so all parameters are editable there, plus single-event query invalidation after save.

title: Standardize branch-aware query keys: eventTypes/metaFields/event caches diverge on working branches
description: Branch-blind keys: MonitoringDetailPage.tsx:86,93,100; settings/ScansTab.tsx:595,219; command-palette.tsx:132. Branch-aware: events/useEventsPageData.ts:25,30,51; settings/EventTypesTab.tsx:49; settings/MetaFieldsTab.tsx:49. Two key shapes coexist ([entity, slug] vs [entity, slug, branchId]); branch-blind consumers fetch main-branch data, so on a working branch parts of the UI show main data while the events list shows branch data, and tab mutations invalidate only branch-aware keys so edits do not propagate until hard reload. Fix: standardize every eventTypes/metaFields/event query and invalidation on [entity, slug, branchId]; thread useActiveBranchId() through MonitoringDetailPage, ScansTab and command-palette and pass branchId into the API calls. Includes the event detail key (MonitoringDetailPage.tsx:86) omitting branchId.
close_reason: Standardized all eventTypes/metaFields/event query keys and invalidations on [entity, slug, branchId]. Threaded useActiveBranchId() through MonitoringDetailPage, ScansTab (incl. CreateMissingFieldsButton + ScanDetail), command-palette and EventDetailPage, passing branchId into the API calls so fetched data matches the key and tab mutations propagate without a hard reload.

title: Rate limiter trusts X-Forwarded-For unconditionally, allowing limit bypass
description: middleware/rate_limit.py:85-94. _client_key takes the leftmost X-Forwarded-For value with no trusted-proxy check. An attacker rotating XFF per request fully bypasses the login/register rate limit, defeating credential-stuffing protection. Fix: add a rate_limit_trust_forwarded_for setting; only honor XFF when enabled, otherwise use request.client.host. Add a spoofed-XFF test.
close_reason: Added rate_limit_trust_forwarded_for setting (default False). _client_key now only honors X-Forwarded-For when the setting is enabled (trusted-proxy deployments); otherwise uses request.client.host, so rotating XFF can no longer spray fresh buckets. Spoofed-XFF test in test_security_middleware.py.

title: Pending alert deliveries stranded if worker dies between commit and dispatch; add reaper beat task
description: worker/tasks/metrics/__init__.py:1588-1596, dispatch.py:160. Deliveries are committed as pending and send_alert_delivery.delay() is enqueued after the outer commit. If the worker crashes between commit and the dispatch loop, or .delay() raises against a down broker, pending deliveries are never dispatched and never retried (cleanup_schema_drifts is the only maintenance task). Fix: add a periodic beat task that re-enqueues AlertDelivery rows stuck in pending older than N minutes, bounded by a max-attempt counter.
close_reason: Added requeue_stranded_alert_deliveries reaper beat task (maintenance.py) that re-enqueues AlertDelivery rows stuck in pending past STRANDED_DELIVERY_MINUTES=15, bounded by dispatch_attempts < MAX_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS=5 (new column + migration 4f5e6d7c8b9a); exhausted rows are marked failed. Registered on a 5-minute beat schedule. Covered by test_requeue_stranded_alert_deliveries_redispatches_and_bounds_attempts.

title: Duplicate alert notifications: acks_late without idempotency guard in send_alert_delivery
description: worker/celery_app.py:25-26, worker/tasks/alerts.py:507-775. With task_acks_late=True and task_reject_on_worker_lost=True, a worker SIGKILLed (OOM/deploy) after _send_telegram_message/_send_jira_issue succeeded but before session.commit() (alerts.py:751) gets the task re-queued and re-executed, re-sending the message or creating a duplicate Jira/Linear ticket. Fix: at the top of send_alert_delivery re-load the delivery and return early if status==sent; for ticket channels store the external id in payload_snapshot and skip creation if present. Add a test calling send_alert_delivery twice on a sent delivery asserting a single external send. Same pattern applies to collect_metrics re-runs.
close_reason: send_alert_delivery now returns early (already_sent) if status==sent. Ticket channels (Jira/Linear) persist external issue id/key into payload_snapshot and skip creation if already present; the id is committed immediately after creation (before the final status=sent commit) so a SIGKILL in that window can't create a duplicate ticket on re-run. _post_json returns the parsed response; _send_jira_issue/_send_linear_issue return (id, key). Tests: idempotent resend (status guard) and skip-creation-when-id-present (crash-window guard).

title: SSRF: webhook/Jira destination URLs accept internal hosts
description: alerting_validation.py:53-69,164-165,235-236. _validate_https_url only checks scheme==https and non-empty netloc. Slack is host-allowlisted but webhook target URLs and Jira base URLs are not: an editor can point a destination at https://169.254.169.254/ (cloud metadata) or internal RFC1918 hosts; the worker (_post_json, alerts.py:225) issues the request from inside the trusted network and surfaces the response body in error_message (blind exfiltration). Fix: add _reject_private_host(parsed.hostname) using ipaddress is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local plus socket.getaddrinfo; reject at validation time AND re-check at send time (DNS rebinding). Add negative tests for private-IP rejection.
close_reason: Added reject_private_host() in alerting_validation.py (ipaddress is_private/loopback/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified + socket.getaddrinfo, fails closed on DNS error). Webhook target URLs and Jira base URLs now reject internal/metadata hosts at validation time via block_private_hosts; re-checked at send time in alerts.py (_reject_private_target) to defend against DNS rebinding. Negative tests for literal private IPs, metadata IP, IPv6 loopback, DNS-resolves-to-private, and fail-closed-on-DNS-error.

description: Implement the 'fact' kind AND fully REMOVE the legacy fact_aggregation (owner: remove entirely, no back-compat). Depends on .1,.2.
notes: Security carry-over from .3 review (MEDIUM, deferred here intentionally): FactTable.columns[].name is stored WITHOUT validate_identifier (validating it in the shared FactTableColumnSchema would break legitimate previews, e.g. a warehouse naming a column 'count()'). The correct injection gate is at the point of USE: in .4 the fact metric's measure_column / distinct_column (and any ratio num/denom columns) reach warehouse SQL unparameterised, so they MUST be validated via validate_identifier at the metric-schema boundary AND constrained to the fact table's introspected column names. This closes the finding where the value actually touches SQL.

title: Metrics: warehouse adapter aggregations + measure/SQL validation
description:

title: Fix incorrect / contradictory ARIA usage
description: ## Fix incorrect / contradictory ARIA usage Part of the frontend WCAG 2.2 AA remediation epic. 8 findings from the verified audit. ### Checklist - [ ] **[HIGH]** `components/settings/kit.tsx`:251-252 (WCAG 4.1.2) — Toggle button has both role="switch" and aria-pressed — contradictory ARIA - The `Toggle` button (line 249) carries `role="switch"` and `aria-pressed={value}` simultaneously. `role="switch"` requires `aria-checked` to express its binary state; `aria-pressed` belongs exclusively to `role="button"`. Screen readers that implement the switch role will ignore `aria-checked` (which is missing) and may announce a confusing or silent state. This fails WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). - **Fix:** Remove `aria-pressed` and keep only `aria-checked={value}` paired with `role="switch"`: ```tsx

title: Announce async status/errors/results via live regions
description:
## Announce async status/errors/results via live regions Part of the frontend WCAG 2.2 AA remediation epic. 15 findings from the verified audit. ### Checklist - [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/AuthPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 4.1.3) — Auth error message not announced to screen readers - When `authMutation.isError` is true, the error `
` at line 184 appears in the DOM silently. Screen readers following focus on the submit button will not be notified of the new error content. The element has no `role="alert"`, `aria-live`, or `aria-errormessage` linkage. - **Fix:** Add `role="alert"` to the error container so it is announced immediately on insertion: ```tsx
{authMutation.error.message}
``` - [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/UsersPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 4.1.3) — Role update error not announced to screen readers - When `updateMut.isError` is true, the error `

` at lines 121–123 is appended to the DOM below the user list. No `role="alert"` or `aria-live` region is present, so screen reader users receive no notification that their role change failed. - **Fix:** Add `role="alert"` to the error paragraph: ```tsx {updateMut.isError && (

{getErrorMessage(updateMut.error)}

)} ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/ui/chart-lazy.tsx`:33-43 (WCAG 4.1.3) — Chart loading fallback is aria-hidden, suppressing status announcement - The `ChartFallback` component applies `aria-hidden` (no value, which coerces to `true`) to the `
` that displays the visible text "Loading…". This means screen readers receive no notification that chart content is loading. Additionally, there is no `role="status"` or `aria-live` region anywhere in the lazy-loaded chart wrappers to announce when the chart finishes loading. Users relying on AT have no indication of the async loading state. - **Fix:** Remove `aria-hidden` from ChartFallback. Add `role="status"` so the loading message is announced as a polite status: `
Loading…
`. If the text is intentionally suppressed visually, replace it with a `Loading chart` inside the container without aria-hidden. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `components/ui/skeleton.tsx`:4-11 (WCAG 4.1.3) — Skeleton loader communicates no loading state to screen readers - The `Skeleton` component renders a pulsing `
` with purely visual feedback (`animate-pulse`). It carries no `aria-busy`, `role="status"`, or hidden text to inform screen reader users that content is loading. When a page section replaces real content with Skeleton placeholders, AT users receive no indication that the page is in a loading state. - **Fix:** Add `aria-busy="true"` and `aria-label="Loading"` to the Skeleton div, or alternatively add a visually-hidden sibling: `Loading…`. At the container level (where multiple skeletons are grouped), prefer wrapping with `
` and making individual Skeleton divs `aria-hidden="true"` to avoid repetitive announcements. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/MonitoringDetailPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 4.1.3) — Mutation error states in annotation form not announced - The `createAnnotationMut` and `deleteAnnotationMut` can fail, but there is no visible or ARIA-announced error message rendered in the annotation panel. Users relying on screen readers will not learn that the mutation failed. - **Fix:** Add an error live region after the form: ```tsx {createAnnotationMut.isError && (

{createAnnotationMut.error?.message ?? 'Failed to add annotation.'}

)} ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/ProjectAlertingTab.tsx`:? (WCAG 4.1.3) — Inbox action mutation error not announced - When `inboxActionMut.isError` is true, the error `

` at lines 383–385 renders inside the Inbox panel with no `role="alert"`. Screen reader users will not be notified that an inbox action (acknowledge, resolve, mute, etc.) failed. - **Fix:** ```tsx {inboxActionMut.isError && (

{getErrorMessage(inboxActionMut.error)}

)} ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/ReconciliationPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 4.1.3) — Shadow event mutation errors not announced - Errors from `acceptMutation` and `dismissMutation` are stored in `rowError[item.id]` and rendered at line 501 as `{error}` with no `role="alert"`. Screen reader users will not be notified when an accept or dismiss action fails. - **Fix:** Change the error span to use `role="alert"`: ```tsx {error && ( {error} )} ``` - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/alerting/DestinationCard.tsx`:437-439 (WCAG 4.1.3) — Mutation error message rendered silently with no live-region announcement - When ruleMutation.isError is true, a

appears (line 438) displaying the error. This change is not inside an aria-live region, so screen reader users who did not have focus on that paragraph will not hear the error after submitting the form. - **Fix:** Add role="alert" (which implies aria-live="assertive") to the error paragraph:

{getErrorMessage(ruleMutation.error)}

. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/alerting/RuleReplayDialog.tsx`:198-202 (WCAG 4.1.3) — Replay error message rendered silently with no live-region announcement - When simulateMut.isError the error
(lines 199-201) appears dynamically but has no role="alert" or aria-live. Screen reader users who triggered Replay will not be notified of the failure. - **Fix:** Add role="alert" to the error container:
Replay failed: {getErrorMessage(simulateMut.error)}
. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/settings-area/ApiKeysSection.tsx`:255-257 (WCAG 4.1.3) — Form submission error in Create Key form not announced to screen readers - `{createMut.isError &&

{getErrorMessage(createMut.error)}

}` is conditionally injected into the DOM on error. This plain `

` has no `role="alert"` or `aria-live`, so screen reader users who submit the form and receive an error will not be notified of the failure. - **Fix:** Change the error paragraph to `

{getErrorMessage(createMut.error)}

`. The `role="alert"` implies `aria-live="assertive"` and will immediately announce the message. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/settings-service/ServiceSettingsPrimitives.tsx`:25-38 (WCAG 4.1.3) — AI connection test result (StatusBadge) is not announced to screen readers - `StatusBadge` appears conditionally after `aiTestMut.data` resolves (AiSection line 102-104), but it is rendered as a plain `` with no `role="status"` or `aria-live` region. When a sighted user clicks "Test AI" and the result appears, a screen reader user receives no announcement of the pass/fail outcome. - **Fix:** Wrap `StatusBadge` in a container with `role="status"` (or `aria-live="polite"`) that is present in the DOM at all times (even when empty): `
{aiTestMut.data && }
`. Place this wrapper in AiSection around line 102. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/settings/ScanDetail.tsx`:249-251 (WCAG 4.1.3) — Apply-groups success status message updates silently without a live region - After a successful `applyGroupsMut` call, the string "Group apply job queued." is rendered into a plain `

` (line 250). Because there is no `role="status"` or `aria-live` on this element or an ancestor, screen readers will not announce this feedback. Users relying on AT will not know the operation succeeded. - **Fix:** Add `role="status"` (which implies `aria-live="polite"`) to the paragraph or a wrapping element that persists in the DOM: ```tsx

{applyGroupsMessage}

``` Keep the element in the DOM even when empty so the live region is registered before the message appears. - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/settings/scans/ReplayDialog.tsx`:82-84 (WCAG 4.1.3) — Mutation error message is not announced to screen readers - When `replayMut.isError` becomes true, a `

` element (line 83) containing the error message is rendered. Because this element has no `role="alert"` or `aria-live` attribute, the error text will not be announced to screen reader users — it will only be visible on screen. - **Fix:** Add `role="alert"` to make the error announced as soon as it appears: ```tsx {replayMut.isError && (

{getErrorMessage(replayMut.error)}

The footer "Showing X–Y of N" text is static markup with no live region, so changes are silent. Keyboard users navigating by filter controls receive no feedback that results have updated. Partially fails WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages). - **Fix:** Add a visually-hidden aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" status region that announces the count when it changes.
