title: Form control label/id association — events, alerting & auth
description:
## Form control label/id association — events, alerting & auth

Part of the frontend WCAG 2.2 AA remediation epic. 21 findings from the verified audit.

### Checklist

- [ ] **[HIGH]** `components/event-photos-section.tsx`:139-149 (WCAG 1.3.1) — Figma URL and title <Input> fields have no labels — placeholder only
    - The two <Input> components at lines 139 and 145 use only placeholder props ('https://www.figma.com/file/…' and 'Title (optional)') as their sole user-visible labels. There are no associated <label> elements, no aria-label, and no aria-labelledby. Placeholders disappear on input and are not a substitute for labels per WCAG 1.3.1 / 3.3.2.
    - **Fix:** Add visible or visually-hidden labels: <label htmlFor="figma-url" className="sr-only">Figma URL</label><Input id="figma-url" placeholder="https://www.figma.com/file/…" ... /> and similarly for the title field.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `components/event-photos-section.tsx`:444-449 (WCAG 1.3.1) — Comment <textarea> has no label — placeholder only
    - The <textarea> at line 444 in CommentThread uses only placeholder="Write a comment…" with no associated <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Screen readers do not reliably announce placeholder text as the control's name, failing WCAG 1.3.1.
    - **Fix:** Add <label htmlFor="comment-body" className="sr-only">Write a comment</label> and id="comment-body" on the <textarea>, or add aria-label="Write a comment" directly to the element.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/DataSourcesPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 1.3.1) — Multiple form inputs in create/edit dialogs lack associated labels
    - In the "New data source" dialog (lines 257–354) and the "Edit data source" dialog (lines 357–415), the `<Label>` elements for Name, Host, Port, Database, Username, Password, Timeout, Project ID, Default dataset, and Service account JSON are NOT linked to their corresponding `<Input>` or `<textarea>` elements via `htmlFor`/`id`. Without this association, screen readers announce the inputs without any label.
    - **Fix:** Add matching `htmlFor` and `id` to every label-input pair. For example:
```tsx
<Label htmlFor="ds-name">Name</Label>
<Input id="ds-name" value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} required ... />

<Label htmlFor="ds-host">Host</Label>
<Input id="ds-host" value={host} ... />
```
Repeat for every field in both create and edit dialogs. The `<select id="ds-type">` already has an `id` and its `<Label htmlFor="ds-type">` is correct — apply the same pattern to all remaining fields.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/MonitoringDetailPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 1.3.1) — Annotation form inputs have no associated labels
    - The annotation creation form at lines 607–639 contains a `datetime-local` input and a text input (lines 615–626) that have no `<label>`, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`. The placeholder text does not substitute for a programmatic label (WCAG 1.3.5, 3.3.2). Screen readers will announce these as unlabeled inputs.
    - **Fix:** Associate visible or visually-hidden labels:
```tsx
<Label htmlFor="annotation-bucket" className="sr-only">Date and time</Label>
<Input
  id="annotation-bucket"
  type="datetime-local"
  ...
/>
<Label htmlFor="annotation-label">Label</Label>
<Input
  id="annotation-label"
  placeholder="Label (e.g. v1.4 deploy)"
  ...
/>
```
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/ProjectAlertingTab.tsx`:? (WCAG 1.3.1) — Audit filter Select elements have no programmatic label association
    - In the Audit panel (lines 391–462), the `<Label>` elements for Status, Channel, Destination, Rule, and Scan are not linked to their corresponding `<Select>` (Radix) triggers via `htmlFor`/`id`. Screen readers will not associate the label text with the combobox control.
    - **Fix:** Add `htmlFor` to each `<Label>` and a matching `id` prop to each `<SelectTrigger>` (Radix SelectTrigger passes unknown props to its underlying `<button>`):
```tsx
<Label htmlFor="filter-status">Status</Label>
<Select ...>
  <SelectTrigger id="filter-status"><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
  ...
</Select>
```
Repeat for Channel, Destination, Rule, and Scan filters.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/ReconciliationPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 1.3.1) — Shadow event type select element has no programmatic label
    - The `<select>` at lines 471–480 in `ShadowRow` that lets users choose an event type for a shadow event has no `<label>`, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`. The adjacent text `<span>` "Choose event type:" is not programmatically associated with the control.
    - **Fix:** Use `aria-label` or a `<label>` element:
```tsx
<label htmlFor={`event-type-select-${item.id}`} className="text-[11px]" style={{ color: 'var(--fg-subtle)' }}>
  Choose event type:
</label>
<select
  id={`event-type-select-${item.id}`}
  className="rounded border px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[11px]"
  value={selectedEventTypeId}
  onChange={(e) => onSelectEventType(e.target.value)}
>
```
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/UsersPage.tsx`:? (WCAG 1.3.1) — Role select element for each user row has no accessible label
    - The `<select>` at lines 97–109 that allows changing a user's role has no `<label>`, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`. When a screen reader reaches this control it announces only the current value and "combobox" with no context identifying which user's role is being changed.
    - **Fix:** Add `aria-label` identifying the user:
```tsx
<select
  value={u.role}
  aria-label={`Role for ${u.name ?? u.email}`}
  onChange={(e) => updateMut.mutate({ userId: u.id, role: e.target.value as Role })}
  ...
>
```
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/DestinationCard.tsx`:251-258 (WCAG 1.3.1) — <Label>Name</Label> not associated with its Input; orphaned Label and floating aria-label
    - The visible <Label>Name</Label> (line 252) has no htmlFor attribute, and the corresponding <Input> has no id — it uses aria-label="Rule Name" instead. This means the visible label is invisible to assistive technology (it does not map to the control), and the accessible name comes only from aria-label which differs slightly from the visible text.
    - **Fix:** Add id="rule-name" to the Input and htmlFor="rule-name" to the Label. Remove the aria-label from Input since the wired Label now provides the accessible name: <Label htmlFor="rule-name">Name</Label><Input id="rule-name" value={ruleForm.name} ... />
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/DestinationCard.tsx`:261-268 (WCAG 1.3.1) — <Label>Cooldown Minutes</Label> not associated with its Input
    - The visible <Label>Cooldown Minutes</Label> has no htmlFor and the <Input type="number"> has no id. The label is programmatically disconnected; screen readers will not announce 'Cooldown Minutes' when the input receives focus.
    - **Fix:** Add id="rule-cooldown" to the Input and htmlFor="rule-cooldown" to the Label.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/DestinationCard.tsx`:354-384 (WCAG 1.3.1) — Three numeric Labels (Min Percent Delta, Min Absolute Delta, Min Expected Count) not associated with their Inputs
    - The three <Label> elements at lines 355, 365, and 375 have no htmlFor and their corresponding <Input type="number"> elements have no id attributes. All three inputs are announced by screen readers without a name.
    - **Fix:** Pair each Label/Input with matching htmlFor/id values, e.g. id="rule-min-pct" / htmlFor="rule-min-pct", id="rule-min-abs" / htmlFor="rule-min-abs", id="rule-min-expected" / htmlFor="rule-min-expected".
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/FilterEditor.tsx`:229 (WCAG 1.3.1) — Search input inside FilterValuePicker popover has no label
    - The <Input placeholder="Search…"> inside FilterValuePicker has no id, no associated <label>, and no aria-label. Placeholder text alone does not satisfy SC 1.3.1/3.3.2 because it disappears once the user types and is not reliably announced by all screen readers.
    - **Fix:** Add aria-label="Search values" to the Input: <Input aria-label="Search values" placeholder="Search…" ... />
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/FilterEditor.tsx`:140-155 (WCAG 1.3.1) — Field and Operator Selects in FilterRow have no accessible label
    - The two <Select> / <SelectTrigger> elements for filter.field and filter.operator are not preceded by any <Label> and have no aria-label. There is no programmatic name for these controls; a screen reader user hears only the current value with no context about what the control configures.
    - **Fix:** Wrap each select with a Radix Label that uses asChild or connect via aria-labelledby. The simplest approach: add aria-label to each SelectTrigger: <SelectTrigger aria-label="Filter field" className="w-36"> and <SelectTrigger aria-label="Filter operator" className="w-24">.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/RuleReplayDialog.tsx`:137-151 (WCAG 1.3.1) — Window Select has a visual <div> label but no programmatic label
    - The 'Window' label is a <div class="text-[11px] uppercase …"> (line 137) not a <label> element and is not connected to the <SelectTrigger> via aria-labelledby or aria-label. The Select's accessible name is empty.
    - **Fix:** Replace the <div> with a visually equivalent <label id="replay-window-label"> and add aria-labelledby="replay-window-label" to the <SelectTrigger>, or add aria-label="Replay window" directly to <SelectTrigger>.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/RuleReplayDialog.tsx`:153-164 (WCAG 1.3.1) — Cooldown override Input has a visual <div> label but no programmatic label
    - The 'Cooldown override (min)' label is a <div class="text-[11px] …"> (line 154) not wired to the <Input> via htmlFor/id or aria-label. The input is announced by screen readers without any name.
    - **Fix:** Replace the <div> with <label htmlFor="replay-cooldown"> and add id="replay-cooldown" to the Input, or add aria-label="Cooldown override in minutes" to the Input directly.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/TemplateEditor.tsx`:70-87 (WCAG 1.3.1) — <Label>Message Format</Label> not associated with the Radix Select
    - The <Label>Message Format</Label> (line 70) has no htmlFor and Radix Select's trigger renders a <button>, not a native <select>. The programmatic label for the format Select is absent; screen readers announce the trigger's current value only.
    - **Fix:** Use Radix <Label asChild> or add a unique id to the SelectTrigger and connect via aria-labelledby: give the Label an id="msg-format-label" and set aria-labelledby="msg-format-label" on the SelectTrigger.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/alerting/TemplateEditor.tsx`:105-129 (WCAG 1.3.1) — <Label>{title}</Label> not associated with the Textarea
    - The <Label> that renders the editor title prop (line 105) has no htmlFor and the <Textarea> (line 129) has no id. The textarea's accessible name is absent; screen readers will not announce what the field is for when it receives focus.
    - **Fix:** Generate a stable id (e.g. using the title prop) and wire them: const textareaId = `template-${title.replace(/\s+/g, '-').toLowerCase()}`; then <Label htmlFor={textareaId}>{title}</Label> and <Textarea id={textareaId} ref={textareaRef} ...>.
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/events/EventForm.tsx`:498-516 (WCAG -) — Field-value controls have no programmatic label association
    - For each field in sortedFields, an <EvField> renders a <label htmlFor={htmlFor}> (line 94) but no htmlFor prop is passed to <EvField> at lines 501-514. The FieldValueControl children (SelectControl, VariableInput, JsonEditor, etc.) are therefore not associated with any <label>. Screen readers will announce these inputs with no label. Fails WCAG 1.3.1 and 3.3.2.
    - **Fix:** Pass htmlFor tied to the field id into EvField and wire the same id to each control. For example:
<EvField key={f.id} label={f.display_name} htmlFor={`field-${f.id}`} ...>
  <FieldValueControl field={f} inputId={`field-${f.id}`} ... />
</EvField>
Then thread inputId through FieldValueControl to SelectControl (id prop) and VariableInput/JsonEditor (id on the underlying <input>/<textarea>).
- [ ] **[HIGH]** `pages/events/EventForm.tsx`:519-536 (WCAG -) — Meta-field controls have no programmatic label association
    - Same pattern as field values: <EvField> for each MetaFieldDefinition does not receive htmlFor (lines 522-534), so the <label> rendered inside EvField has no for attribute and is not programmatically associated with the MetaFieldControl's <select> or <input>. Screen readers announce these controls with no label. Fails WCAG 1.3.1 and 3.3.2.
    - **Fix:** Pass htmlFor={`meta-${mf.id}`} to EvField and pass a matching id prop down through MetaFieldControl to the underlying SelectControl (id prop) and VariableInput (id on the inner <Input>).
- [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/ProjectAlertingTab.tsx`:? (WCAG 1.3.1) — Destination form Label elements not linked to their inputs
    - Throughout the destination create/edit form (lines 504–758), `<Label>` components such as "Name" (line 508), "Channel" (line 516), "Webhook URL" (line 537), "Bot Token" (line 551), "Chat ID" (line 562), and all other channel-specific fields are rendered without `htmlFor` attributes. The paired `<Input>` and `<Select>` elements also lack `id` attributes. The only exception is the `aria-label` duplicating the visible label on each `<Input>`, which helps AT but does not create the programmatic association needed for click-to-focus and correct label announcement.
    - **Fix:** Add matching `htmlFor`/`id` pairs to every label-input/select pair. For example:
```tsx
<Label htmlFor="dest-name">Name</Label>
<Input
  id="dest-name"
  aria-label="Destination Name"
  value={destinationForm.name}
  ...
/>
<Label htmlFor="dest-channel">Channel</Label>
<Select ...>
  <SelectTrigger id="dest-channel"><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
  ...
</Select>
```
Repeat for all other fields; remove the redundant `aria-label` once `htmlFor`/`id` is correct.
- [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/events/EventsToolbar.tsx`:74-91 (WCAG -) — Search input has no accessible label — placeholder is the only label
    - The <Input> at line 78 uses placeholder="Filter by name, tag, field…" as its sole label. There is no visible <label> element and no aria-label attribute. Placeholders disappear on input and are not a sufficient substitute for labels under WCAG 1.3.1 and 3.3.2. The decorative <Search> icon (line 75) is not aria-hidden and may be announced by screen readers as an image.
    - **Fix:** Add aria-label="Filter events by name, tag, or field" to the <Input>. Also add aria-hidden="true" to the decorative <Search> icon since it duplicates the placeholder intent:
<Search className="..." aria-hidden="true" />
<Input aria-label="Filter events by name, tag, or field" placeholder="Filter by name, tag, field…" ... />
- [ ] **[MEDIUM]** `pages/events/TabMetricsCard.tsx`:128-137 (WCAG -) — Granularity SelectTrigger has no accessible label
    - The <SelectTrigger className="h-7 w-28 text-xs"> at line 132 has neither aria-label nor an associated visible <label>. Its only content is <SelectValue /> which renders the current selection. Screen readers will announce it as a generic combobox with the value but no label describing what the control selects. The Status and Activity selects in EventsToolbar have aria-label; this one is missing it. Fails WCAG 1.3.1 and 3.3.2.
    - **Fix:** Add aria-label="Granularity" (or "Time granularity") to the SelectTrigger:
<SelectTrigger className="h-7 w-28 text-xs" aria-label="Time granularity">

### Acceptance
- All checklist items addressed in code
- `pnpm lint` passes (jsx-a11y rules) and relevant `pnpm test` axe assertions green
close_reason: Fixed via audit+remediation workflow; verified by tsc/lint/test/build gates.

title: Bound query params and list limits (metrics, data_sources, events, users)
description:
MEDIUM — input validation (routers reviewer). Several numeric params are unbounded, risking heavy DB aggregation / memory:
- metrics.py: `days` (l.85), `window_hours`+`limit` (l.97-98), `limit` (l.220) — no upper bound. Wrap in `Query(..., ge=1, le=<max>)` e.g. days le=365, window_hours le=720, limit le=100.
- data_sources.py:59 `window_hours: int = 48` — same fix.
- events.py:38 `limit` allows `le=10000` while each event eager-loads field_values/meta_values/tags/variable_values via selectin → memory/DoS. Lower to le=500/1000; add a dedicated async export endpoint if bulk export is a real need.
- users.py:17 `list_users` has no LIMIT/offset. Add `limit`/`offset` Query params for consistency.
close_reason: Done: bounded metrics/data_sources/events/users query params + list ceilings (events 10000->1000, users pagination). test_query_bounds added. Green.

title: Startup hardening: detect default creds + wildcard CORS; configure logging at import; freeze Settings
description:
MEDIUM — config/startup (app-core reviewer). Three related items:
1. `config.assert_production_ready()` validates encryption_key/cookie/CORS-empty but NEVER checks whether `database_url`/`sync_database_url`/`rabbitmq_url` still carry their dev-credential defaults (`tripl:tripl`, `guest:guest`, config.py:8-10) — a misconfigured prod deploy silently runs on dev creds. Add checks that flag the literal default user/pass.
2. Same guard passes when `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=*` is set explicitly (returns `["*"]`, non-empty). The wildcard silently disables cookie auth (main.py:76 handles it correctly) but with no startup warning. Add a problem/warn when `cors_origins() == ["*"]` in non-debug, and a `logger.warning` when the credential fallback activates.
3. `configure_logging()` runs only inside the async lifespan (main.py:28), so module-import-time logs (router mount, tracing, test collection) use default logging. Move `configure_logging()` to module level before `app = FastAPI(...)`, keep the lifespan call as an idempotent re-apply.
4. (Optional) `Settings` is a mutable module singleton; tests mutate fields directly (conftest.py:12, test_security_middleware.py). Consider `frozen=True` + `monkeypatch.setattr` in tests so mutations roll back.
close_reason: Done: assert_production_ready flags default DB/RabbitMQ creds, wildcard CORS, and missing secret_key; configure_logging moved to import time. frozen=True DEFERRED (see follow-up). Green.

title: Configure async DB engine pool (pool_pre_ping, pool_recycle, pool_size/max_overflow)
description:
MEDIUM — confirmed (2 reviewers). `database.py:7 create_async_engine(...)` is called with only `echo=settings.debug`. The worker's sync engine (worker/db.py:31-37) explicitly sets `pool_size=5, max_overflow=10, pool_pre_ping=True, pool_recycle=1800`. Without `pool_pre_ping`/`pool_recycle`, connections idled out by the DB/LB surface as OperationalError/asyncpg errors on the first request that checks out a dead connection in long-lived deployments.

Fix: add `pool_pre_ping=True, pool_recycle=1800` and explicit `pool_size`/`max_overflow` to `create_async_engine`, matching the worker.
close_reason: Done: async create_async_engine now sets pool_pre_ping/pool_recycle=1800/pool_size/max_overflow matching the worker. test_db_engine added. Green.

title: Crypto hardening: raise scrypt cost + rehash-on-login; HMAC session-token hashing
description:
MEDIUM — hardening (security reviewer). Two items in auth_utils.py:
1. `SCRYPT_N = 2**14` (auth_utils.py:8) is below the OWASP scrypt recommendation (N=2**17, r=8, p=1). Stored hashes embed their params, so raising the constant won't upgrade existing hashes. Fix: raise to >=2**17 AND add a rehash-on-successful-login path in `authenticate_user` that detects a stored N below the current minimum and re-hashes.
2. `hash_session_token` (auth_utils.py:64) uses bare `hashlib.sha256`. Tokens are 32-byte `secrets.token_urlsafe` (adequate entropy), but switching to `hmac.new(settings.secret_key, token, sha256)` makes a leaked session table useless without the app secret — same defense already applied to the Fernet encryption key. Requires adding/confirming a SECRET_KEY setting. (Lower priority than #1; migration: dual-read old+new during rollover or invalidate sessions.)
close_reason: Done: scrypt N 2**14->2**16 (memory-balanced for ARM SBC) + rehash-on-login; session tokens now HMAC-SHA256 keyed by settings.secret_key. NOTE: existing sessions invalidated on deploy (one re-login). Green.

title: /health: stop leaking DB error detail to unauthenticated callers
description:

close_reason: Done: /health returns generic {status:error,component:database}, logs exception server-side; no DSN/exc leak. Test added. Green.

title: P2 — Restore the scan Replay entry point (replay button missing)
description:
## P2 — Restore the scan Replay entry point ("кнопка реплея пропала") **Defect (reported):** the Replay button disappeared from a scan. ### Current behavior / root cause The button and the replay feature both still exist. After the modal→inline refactor (tripl-f7q6.15), the inline Replay panel (`ReplayDialog`, now an in-flow `
` with `if (!open) return null`) is rendered at the **top** of the Configuration tab (`ScanConfigForm.tsx:99-104`), while the **"Replay…" trigger button** lives at the **bottom**, in the Danger-zone card (`ScanConfigForm.tsx:116-161`, button at 129-139). Clicking the button toggles `replayOpen` and the panel opens detached/off-screen above all the form cards — in the real browser nothing visibly happens, so the feature appears gone. (jsdom has no viewport, so the existing test at `ProjectSettingsPage.test.tsx:478-498` still passes — it locates the panel by role, not position.) ### Proposed fix (single-file JSX relocation, **zero deps**) Keep the existing button, the `ReplayDialog` component, and the API; only render the panel next to its trigger inside the Danger zone. 1. `ScanConfigForm.tsx` — remove the top-level `` block at lines 99-104. Leave `{dialog}` (98) and the `replayOpen`/`setReplayOpen` state (line 36) untouched. 2. Render `ReplayDialog` **inside** the Danger-zone `SCard` (lines 116-161), immediately after the "Run a one-off replay" row (the div at 117-140) and before the Delete row (141), so it expands directly beneath the button: ```tsx {replayOpen && (
)} ``` Wrapper padding/border matches sibling rows so the panel reads as part of the Danger-zone card. 3. Make the trigger a toggle (polish, recommended): button onClick → `setReplayOpen(o => !o)`; optionally `variant={replayOpen ? 'default' : 'outline'}`. **Keep as-is:** entry button label `"Replay…"`, `variant="outline"`, `size="sm"`, leading ``, gated by `canReplay = Boolean(scanConfig.time_column && scanConfig.interval)` with its title→(prefer aria) tooltip (`ScanConfigForm.tsx:68,129-139`). Panel submit keeps `"Replay period"`/`"Starting…"` + filled accent variant (`ReplayDialog.tsx:87-90`). **Do NOT reintroduce a modal Dialog** — the redesign's "everything is a page/inline, no modals" rule is satisfied by the in-flow section; the only requirement is rendering it in place. API/route unchanged: `scansApi.replayMetrics` → POST `/projects/{slug}/scans/{scanId}/metrics/replay` (`api/scans.ts:118-121`; backend `scans.py:162-167`). ### Acceptance criteria - In the running app: Scan detail → Edit/Configuration tab → Danger zone → click "Replay…" → the Replay panel appears immediately beneath the "Run a one-off replay" row (not at the top of the page), visible without scrolling away. - From/To datetime-local inputs + "Replay period" submit are reachable; submit still POSTs `{time_from,time_to}` ISO strings, closes the panel, and invalidates scanJobs/scans queries. - "Replay…" stays disabled with its "Requires time column and interval" tooltip when time_column or interval is missing. - `ReplayDialog` is no longer rendered at the top of the Configuration tab. - `pnpm test` (existing ProjectSettingsPage.test.tsx replay test green), `pnpm lint` (zero warnings), `pnpm build` pass. ### Open questions - Toggle-on-second-click + variant-reflects-state: in scope as recommended polish, or leave one-way open? (Decide so the optional document-order test guard is/ isn't added.) - Long-term home: keep in Danger zone (current redesign/tests), or promote Replay near the "Run now" header action (`ScanConfigDetailView.tsx:91-94`)? Promotion is a larger UX change — out of this fix. **Risk:** Low — single-file JSX relocation; no API/route/component-contract change. ReplayDialog already calls `onOpenChange(false)` on success, so the toggle won't get stuck open.

Settings becomes a **dedicated full-takeover area** (Linear/Vercel pattern), holding only

Branches, Audit, Coverage) is a first-class sidebar page now — the old 11-tab

- **Project · tripl-web**

    color swatches) + Defaults (default branch, environment, timezone) + Danger zone (Archive /
    Transfer ownership / Delete with consequence copy).

    pattern regex) + Governance (require review, require owner, min approvals, auto-deprecate
    dormant) + PII & compliance (detect PII, block PII without consent, raw event retention).
- **Workspace · Windy Labs**
  - Members: members list (avatar, email, role select or Owner chip, last active, manage) +
    pending invitations (resend / revoke); "Invite".
  - Data sources: connected sources (icon, status dot, throughput sparkline, events count,
    Configure) + "Add a source" grid (iOS/Android/Web/Server).
  - API keys: warning banner ("shown once"), active keys (key icon, name, masked prefix, scope
    chip, created, used, copy/revoke); "Create key".
- **Account · You**
  - Profile: avatar (upload/remove), full name, email, role chip; Preferences (timezone, date
    format, start of week); Notifications toggles (incident alerts, review requests, weekly
    digest).
  - Security: Password (current/new + update); 2FA (authenticator toggle, recovery codes
    regenerate); Active sessions (device list with revoke, "Sign out all").
- **Instance (owner only)** — mirror real `ServiceSettings` sections: Runtime (server, ingest),
  Email (SMTP, sender), AI (provider/model/key + limits), Security & access (SSO, domains,
  session length; network IP allowlist), Storage (object storage backend/bucket/region;
  retention), Observability (Prometheus, tracing, log level; Sentry), System (read-only status,
  build `InfoRow`s, license).

### Acceptance
- Settings is a full-takeover area with a working Project/Workspace switch and grouped rail;
  only configuration lives here (functional surfaces stay in the sidebar). All sections match
  the mockup and reuse the shared control kit. Owner-only Instance sections gated by role.

Implement the Claude Design handoff for Tripl (design hash Id_gRuGqMcA7Gg3N-1kGaQ, Tripl.html). The design assistant audited the real frontend and concluded the codebase is already well-built (mature oklch tokens, virtualized events table, command palette, branch switcher, activity panel, tweaks) — the ONE real weakness is information architecture: the global nav is flat (Main / Settings + a Projects list + a Views list), which buries high-value surfaces (Monitoring, Alerting, Audit, Reconciliation, Data sources) under Settings tabs.

The fix: replace the flat nav with four job-based groups, giving every major feature a first-class home, project-scoped, with the project switcher at top and org-level Settings folded into the footer.

Groups (mapped only to surfaces that ALREADY exist as routes — no invented pages):
- PLAN: Events (/p/:slug/events), Event types (/settings/event-types), Schema & fields (/settings/meta-fields), Plan branches (/settings/branches)
- OBSERVE: Monitors (/settings/monitoring), Alerting (/settings/alerting)
- GOVERN: Reconciliation (/p/:slug/reconciliation), Audit log (/settings/audit)
- CONNECT: Data sources (/settings/data-sources)

Footer: user + org Settings + project settings + sign out. Counts/tones (danger/warning dots) on items where cheap project-summary data exists. Collapsed rail mirrors the groups with separators. Preserve existing tokens, density, command palette, branch switcher, activity panel.

Scope guard: do NOT invent backend-less surfaces (Anomalies, Coverage, Destinations page, API keys) — fold them into nearest real surface or omit; note decisions per sub-issue.

Requires migration of the existing boolean fields and UI updates everywhere event state is shown/edited.

Violations become a new drift type flowing through the existing schema_drifts + alerting pipeline (delivery channels already work). Highest value for lowest new infrastructure: PSI, drift model and alerting are all reused; the catalog becomes an enforceable data contract.
close_reason: Closed

title: Plan-reality reconciliation: shadow events inbox, dead events report, coverage metric
description: Today scans GENERATE events from warehouse data but never answer the core tracking-plan question: how well does the plan match reality. Three parts. 1) Shadow events inbox: scan actively detects events present in warehouse data but absent from the plan and puts them into an inbox with an auto-drafted schema (fields from observed columns/JSON paths, matched against existing variables); an analyst accepts into the plan (via a working branch) or dismisses. 2) Dead events report: events with implemented=true not seen in data for N days (last_seen_at exists but is a passive label with no workflow). 3) Coverage metric: percent of warehouse event volume covered by the plan, trended over time. Foundation already exists: scans, source_name identity, last_seen_at. Turns the catalog from documentation into a living reconciliation.
close_reason: Reconciliation v1 shipped: shadow events inbox (collector flags warehouse identities missing from plan, accept creates a matching event, dismiss persists), dead events report (implemented but unseen for N days, grace period for new events), per-bucket coverage metric (matched vs total warehouse volume) with API and compact frontend page. title: Warehouse adapters: wire DataSource.timeout_seconds, connect_timeout, statement_timeout, TLS
description: worker/adapters/postgres.py:45-52, clickhouse.py:28-35. psycopg.connect uses autocommit=True with no sslmode and no statement_timeout; a user-supplied base_query can run unbounded until the 55/60-min Celery hard limit SIGKILLs the worker. ClickHouse client takes no connect_timeout/send_receive_timeout. DataSource.timeout_seconds exists but the constructors ignore it (confirm wiring in registry.build_adapter). Tests in test_adapter_registry.py.

title: get_session dependency lacks rollback on exception; add global exception handler

Fix: wrap yield in try/except, rollback and re-raise. Related: main.py has no global FastAPI exception handler; add one that rolls back and emits a request-id-tagged structured log.
close_reason: get_session wraps yield in try/except with rollback + re-raise so an aborted transaction can't return to the pool; added a global FastAPI exception handler that logs with the request id and returns a generic 500. Tests in test_error_handling.py.

Fix: delete UserSession rows on role downgrade so the next request re-auths; document the short staleness window.

title: Tracking plan versioning + diff
description:
Snapshot the entire tracking plan (event types, field definitions, relations, meta fields, variables, events) into immutable plan_revision rows so users can see when the schema changed and what changed.

MVP scope:
1. plan_revisions table + Alembic migration: id, project_id (FK), created_at, created_by (FK to users, nullable), summary (text), payload (JSON snapshot of the project schema).
2. Service: build_plan_snapshot(project_id) constructs the payload from current rows; create_revision persists it.
3. API:
   - POST /projects/{slug}/revisions — manual snapshot, optional summary
   - GET /projects/{slug}/revisions — list (paginated)
   - GET /projects/{slug}/revisions/{id} — full detail
   - GET /projects/{slug}/revisions/{id}/diff?compare_to={other_id} — entity-level diff (added/removed/changed)
4. Frontend: /p/:slug/settings/history tab — table of revisions with timestamps and authors, click to expand a diff against the previous revision, 'Snapshot now' button with optional note.

Out of scope for MVP: auto-snapshot on every mutation, breaking-change alert scope, approval workflow, rollback action.
design: Payload shape: { event_types: [...], events: [...], variables: [...], meta_fields: [...], relations: [...] }. Each entity carries only the fields that affect downstream consumers (name, display_name, field_type, is_required, enum_options, etc.) — created_at / updated_at / order / UUIDs go through so we can stable-sort but aren't compared for diff purposes. Diff is computed in Python over the two payloads using a small set-difference helper per entity type. No re-query at diff time — payload-vs-payload makes the diff deterministic even after later deletes.
close_reason: New plan_revisions table (Alembic 9e0f1a2b3c4d). build_plan_snapshot constructs deterministic JSON over event types + field definitions + events + variables + meta fields + relations (sorted by natural key, UUIDs / order / timestamps excluded from comparison fields). compute_plan_diff_entries does natural-key set difference per entity type, surfaces field-level changes for the fields that matter (field_type, is_required, enum_options, implemented/reviewed/archived, etc.). API: POST/GET /projects/{slug}/revisions, GET /revisions/{id}, GET /revisions/{id}/diff?compare_to={other}. Frontend: HistoryTab in ProjectSettingsPage with revision list + 'Snapshot now' button + side-by-side diff against previous revision. Tests: 176 backend (+3 — snapshot composition, diff classification, full POST→GET→diff round-trip), 33 frontend. ruff+mypy+tsc+eslint clean.

description:
Two simulator extensions:

1) Live preview: render each simulated firing through the rule's actual message_template + items_template so the user sees the exact Slack/Telegram text that would have been sent. Reuses existing alert_templates render path; no DB writes.

2) Cooldown A/B: in the Replay dialog, let the user override cooldown_minutes (slider) without saving the rule. Endpoint accepts ?cooldown_minutes_override=N and runs simulate_rule_firings with the override. UI shows side-by-side: 'current K firings' vs 'with override M firings'.
design:
Preview: extend SimulatedRuleFiring with rendered_item (string) and AlertRuleSimulateResponse with rendered_message (string). Build a fake AlertDeliveryItem-shaped dict per firing, feed into _build_item_template_context-equivalent. Reuse the no_autoflush pattern for sparkline/top_movers — same call site.

A/B: simulate_rule signature gets optional cooldown_minutes_override; if set, replace rule.cooldown_minutes for the duration of the call. Frontend renders two columns when override differs from saved value.
close_reason: simulate_rule_firings accepts cooldown_minutes_override (keyword-only). simulate_rule service: _render_firing_item + _render_firings_message build a sync preview reusing alert_templates (no DB-bound sparkline/top_movers — those are session-rich and out of scope for replay). New response fields: rendered_message (overall message text), per-firing rendered_item, cooldown_minutes_used, cooldown_minutes_saved. API endpoint exposes cooldown_minutes_override query param (0..10080). Frontend: RuleReplayDialog gets cooldown override Input; on Replay issues Promise.all(saved, override) when override differs, shows side-by-side FiringsCountBadge with both counts and Noisy flag, plus a Preview <pre> block of rendered_message. Tests: 173 backend (+1 — endpoint asserts override path + preview text), 33 frontend, ruff+mypy+tsc+eslint clean.

title: Schema drift: retention cleanup job + sample values
description:
Two follow-ups to the schema-drift v1:

1) Add a Celery beat job that DELETEs SchemaDrift rows past DRIFT_RETENTION_DAYS (currently we only filter on read — the table grows forever).

2) Capture a sample value when we detect new_field / type_changed drift. The cardinality analyzer already has sample values per column; thread them through _diff_event_type_schema -> _upsert_schema_drifts -> SchemaDrift.sample_value. Surface in drift API and badge popover.
design:
Cleanup: new task tripl.worker.tasks.maintenance.cleanup_schema_drifts on a daily schedule. DELETE WHERE detected_at < now() - 30 days. Small footprint, idempotent.

Sample value: CardinalityResult.sample_values is list[str]; take first non-empty value, truncate at 255 chars. type_changed already records observed/declared types, we just attach an example. missing_field doesn't get a sample (no observed data) — keep null.
close_reason: Added _pick_sample_value helper that threads CardinalityResult.sample_values into _diff_event_type_schema for new_field/type_changed drift (missing_field stays null — no observed data). _upsert_schema_drifts persists sample_value and refreshes it on conflict. Both call sites in metrics.py pass cardinality results defensively via getattr to keep mock-based unit tests working. New tripl.worker.tasks.maintenance.cleanup_schema_drifts task + daily Celery beat schedule prunes SchemaDrift rows past DRIFT_RETENTION_DAYS. UI: EventDriftBadge popover renders 'e.g. <sample>' under each drift entry. Tests: 172 backend (+2), ruff+mypy clean.

title: Anomaly explainability: sparkline + top movers in alert delivery
description:
When an anomaly is delivered to Slack or Telegram, the payload should include (a) a sparkline for the last 24 buckets for the scope and (b) the top 3 movers: breakdown values with the largest deviation from expected, so the recipient can see immediately what changed and why.

Scope:
1. tripl/anomaly_context.py: build_sparkline(points, width=24), top_movers_for_anomaly(session, anomaly, limit=3).
2. Hook into _build_delivery_snapshot: pass sparkline and top_movers into each item snapshot.
3. alert_templates.py: add sparkline and top_movers to ALERT_ITEM_TEMPLATE_VARIABLES, and add them to default item templates for each format.
4. Tests: sparkline rendering, top_movers ranking by abs(z_score), end-to-end delivery snapshot.
design:
Reuse MetricBreakdownAnomaly: it already computes per-(column,value) anomalies. top_movers is a query against metric_breakdown_anomalies for the matching scope and anomaly bucket, ordered by abs(z_score) descending, limited to 3. No extra ClickHouse load.

Sparkline is pure functional: reads EventMetric for the last N buckets for the scope and maps values to 8 Unicode blocks. It is safe for all 4 message formats because the same characters are used.
close_reason: anomaly_context.py: build_sparkline (8-block Unicode, width=24), format_top_movers (signed %, +inf% guard, value truncation), load_top_movers ordered by abs(z_score), and load_recent_metric_points for project_total/event_type/event. Wired through _build_item_template_context -> _build_items_text -> _build_template_context -> _render_delivery_message with optional session+scan_config_id. New vars: sparkline, top_movers, sparkline_line, top_movers_line. Updated default item templates. session.no_autoflush is critical because otherwise SELECT triggers autoflush on the JSON column and loses later in-place payload_snapshot mutations. Tests: 168 backend (+3 explainability), ruff and mypy clean.

title: SchemaDrift model + cardinality compare + drift API + UI badge
description:
Extend the cardinality analyzer: for a known event, compare the current field set with FieldDefinition and write SchemaDrift records. UI: red drift badge on EventRow plus a drill-down popover with examples.

Scope:
1. Alembic migration: schema_drifts(id, event_id, field_name, drift_type, detected_at, sample_value, scan_config_id).
2. SchemaDrift model + Event.schema_drifts relationship.
3. Cardinality analyzer writes drift records inside the metrics pipeline after event generation.
4. drift_type enum: new_field, missing_field, type_changed.
5. Retention: clean up drifts older than 30 days in check_metrics_due or a new task.
6. API: GET /projects/{slug}/events/{event_id}/drifts.
7. EventListItem.drift_count in list responses as an aggregate, not the full list.
8. Frontend: drift badge on EventRow with count; click opens a popover with the latest N records.
design:
Drift detection lives in the metrics pipeline, not a separate task: we already have the cardinality analysis result and the match to event_id, so a second pass is unnecessary. Comparison is current column_names vs FieldDefinition.name for the event type using two set differences.

drift_count in list response is a separate COUNT subquery over schema_drifts with 30d retention. This avoids sending a full list payload for catalogs with 1000+ events.
close_reason: Added schema_drifts table, migration, model, and 30d retention. _diff_event_type_schema detects new_field, missing_field, and type_changed; type_changed only applies to auto-created string/json types, so user-curated enum/number/url/boolean fields are not disturbed. Added a metrics pipeline hook before _ensure_event_type_with_fields. Added GET /event-types/{id}/drifts. EventListItem.drift_count is included through a single-query list_events path. UI adds EventDriftBadge on EventRow with details popover. Tests: drift diff unit test (3 types plus idempotent upsert), all tests green.

title: Alert rule simulate endpoint + UI Replay modal
description:
POST /alert-destinations/{dest_id}/rules/{rule_id}/simulate?days=7 walks MetricAnomaly over the selected window and returns virtual deliveries without writing to the DB. UI: a Replay 7d button next to a rule in ProjectAlertingTab opens a modal with bucket, scope, anomaly delta, and rendered template.

Scope:
1. alerting_service: extract _evaluate_rule(rule, anomaly_iter, dry_run) as one path for the live pipeline and simulator.
2. POST /alert-destinations/{dest_id}/rules/{rule_id}/simulate endpoint.
3. Pydantic SimulatedDeliveryResponse: bucket, scope_type, scope_ref, anomaly_id, actual_count, expected_count, z_score, rendered_message.
4. Frontend: Replay button in ProjectAlertingTab -> modal list + warning when the rule is too noisy (>50 matches in the window).
design: Existing pipeline matching is: pull anomalies, check rule filters, gate through cooldown, enqueue delivery. Extract a pure simulate_rule(session, rule, days) function that returns list[SimulatedDelivery]. Cooldown is simulated in memory with a sorted pass and last_fired_at. The template is rendered through the same alert_templates.py code, which guarantees preview equals real delivery.
close_reason: alerting_matching.py: pure rule_matches_anomaly plus simulate_rule_firings with in-memory cooldown and per-scope partitioning. The metrics worker uses the same path. Added POST /alert-destinations/{id}/rules/{id}/simulate?days=N and Pydantic schemas. UI: History button on each rule plus RuleReplayDialog with firings table and noisy warning. Tests: 3 backend tests (matcher cooldown, scope filter, endpoint), all backend (164) and frontend (31) tests green.

title: Event.last_seen_at + Last seen UI column with silent filter
description:
Add Event.last_seen_at (nullable timestamptz). Update it from the metrics pipeline when a bucket has a non-zero count. Show it in EventsPage as a relative-time column and add a Silent > 7d filter.

This is the first atomic step toward the schema drift detector. It is valuable by itself and reduces the risk of one large migration.

Scope:
1. Alembic migration: nullable event.last_seen_at timestamptz.
2. Event model: add the field.
3. Metrics pipeline writer updates last_seen_at = MAX(bucket_ts) when count > 0.
4. Pydantic Event schema: add last_seen_at.
5. EventsPage: new Last seen relative-time column in ColumnsMenu, hidden by default.
6. Toolbar filter: Silent > 7d/30d/never.
7. Backend filter in /events list: silent_since_days query param.
design:
The metrics pipeline already knows event_id and bucket_ts. A single UPDATE in the same transaction as event_metrics insert is enough.

The frontend sends ?silent_since_days=7; the backend translates it to WHERE (last_seen_at IS NULL OR last_seen_at < now() - interval 7 days).
close_reason: Added Event.last_seen_at via migration, bumped it in the metrics writer (monotonic, ignores count=0), added silent_since_days API filtering, and added the Last seen catalog column (hidden by default with bootstrap) plus toolbar select options for Silent > 1d/7d/30d. Tests: 161 backend, 31 frontend, ruff and mypy clean.

title: Split EventsPage.tsx into focused pieces + saved views + command palette
description:
EventsPage.tsx is 1367 lines and currently owns filters, virtualization, metrics, and selection. It is the main product page, and the current structure makes it hard to add features such as saved views, bulk edit, and a sparkline column.

Scope:
1. useEventsQuery hook for filters, sort, pagination, and URL sync.
2. EventsToolbar component for search, statuses, tags, columns menu, and view switcher.
3. EventsTable component for virtualization and DnD reorder.
4. EventsPage.tsx becomes a host component of 300 lines or fewer.
5. Saved views: localStorage model (project_slug -> name -> filter snapshot) and UI to save/load/delete.
6. Command palette (Cmd+K) using cmdk-react for events, event types, scans, and settings tab navigation.
design:
Make the split regression-safe: existing tests in EventsPage.test.tsx should pass unchanged after each refactor step. Saved views are pure client-side first with localStorage; server-side persistence can be added later when auth exists.

Command palette is isolated as one CommandMenu component in App.tsx. It opens with Cmd+K and fetches data through existing query hooks with staleTime=5min.
notes:
Progress 2026-05-15: added pure-client saved views for EventsPage. Current tab + URL search params are stored per project slug in localStorage; toolbar has Views popover to save/apply/delete; storage helper covered by Vitest.

The page still owns URL-backed filter state, saved-view state, and column visibility callbacks; the toolbar is now a presentational component over those props. Remaining scope: extract useEventsQuery, extract EventsTable, add command palette, and continue shrinking EventsPage.tsx toward the host-component target.

title: Alert rule simulator (replay last 7 days)
description:
Alert rules are currently tuned blind: to know whether a rule will fire, the user has to wait for a real anomaly. Add a Replay button directly in the rule form that shows how many times the rule would have fired over the last N days, which events triggered it, and the cooldown effect.

Scope:
1. POST /alert-rules/{id}/simulate?days=7 walks MetricAnomaly over the window, applies rule filters and cooldown, and returns a list of virtual deliveries.
2. Pure function in alerting_service: rule + anomalies -> simulated_deliveries, without writing to DB.
3. UI in ProjectAlertingTab: Replay 7d button next to a rule -> modal list with timestamp, event_type, anomaly delta, and rendered template.
4. Highlight when simulation returns >50 firings in the window with a warning that the rule is too noisy.
design:
Matching logic must be exactly the same as the live pipeline. Extract it into alerting_service._evaluate_rule(rule, anomaly_iter, dry_run: bool) so both the live taskcall and simulate use one path.

Cooldown is simulated in memory: last_fired_at advances through sorted anomaly items.
close_reason: Parent scope is complete via tripl-wtu: shared rule matcher, simulate endpoint, Replay UI modal, noisy warning, and tests are present.

title: Schema drift detector + last-seen in catalog
description:
Event implementation status is currently set manually, and differences between the declared schema and real ClickHouse data are only visible through manual scan-result inspection.

Goal: automatically maintain last-seen for each Event and raise SchemaDrift when known-event data gains new fields or changes dominant type. This becomes the primary signal that the catalog diverged from production.

Scope:
1. Event.last_seen_at (nullable timestamptz) + migration.
2. Metrics pipeline updates last_seen_at for non-zero counts in the window.
3. last seen column in EventsPage + silent > 7d filter.
4. SchemaDrift model (event_id, field_name, drift_type, detected_at, sample_value).
5. Cardinality analyzer compares current fields with FieldDefinition and writes drift records.
6. Anomaly scope=schema flows into the alert pipeline.
7. UI: drift badge on EventRow + drill-down with examples.
design:
Do not duplicate metric tables. last_seen_at is just a projection, updated in the same transaction as event_metrics insert. SchemaDrift is a separate table because it has its own retention; 30 days is enough.

Alert pipeline already knows scope=project/event_type/event; add schema as a fourth scope. alert_templates.py receives variables drift_field, drift_type, and sample_value.
close_reason: Completed remaining parent scope: schema drifts now have an alert scope flag, live delivery/replay candidates, template variables drift_field/drift_type/sample_value/drift_line, UI rule toggle, migration, and tests.

title: Propagate request_id FE->BE, surface to users, bind to OTEL trace
description: Backend assigns/echoes X-Request-ID (middleware/request_id.py:36-64) and embeds request_id in 500 bodies, but FE never sends the header, never reads/displays it, and OTEL trace_id is not bound to request_id -> two disjoint correlation namespaces; users cannot quote a correlation id on errors. Also 403 is not distinguished from generic errors (only 401 re-auths), and 502/503/504 collapse to a fixed message masking real 503 bodies. Fix: send crypto.randomUUID X-Request-ID from client.ts, surface body.request_id on 5xx, set request_id as OTEL span attribute, handle 403/503 explicitly.

title: Decide: PEP 758 unparenthesized 'except A, B:' — keep (3.14 feature) vs parenthesize (portability)

Identical AST/behavior on 3.14, zero warnings. Tradeoff: KEEP embraces the flagship 3.14 syntax; PARENTHESIZE removes two footguns — (a) hard SyntaxError if any tooling/CI/pre-commit/editor parses these on Python <3.14, (b) visual resemblance to the Python-2 'except E, var:' binding form. Recommendation: parenthesize for portability + readability (pure style, no behavior change). Awaiting owner decision.

title: Test hygiene: dispose conftest async engine to clear 32 ResourceWarnings
description: pytest emits 32 ResourceWarning 'unclosed database' (sqlite3) because conftest.py's module-global async engine is never disposed. Add a session-scoped teardown that awaits engine.dispose() (or use NullPool for the test engine) so connections close deterministically.

notes: PARTIAL + RESCOPED. Done: shared conftest async engine is now disposed at session end (the 4 data-layer files that previously warned now show 0 ResourceWarnings in isolation). Full fix = audit each create_engine site and guarantee dispose (try/finally or fixture). Benign (542 pass), pre-existing, orthogonal to Python 3.14 correctness — deferred to avoid disproportionate churn. Verify cheaply by running just those 5 files with -W default.

Full suite: 542 passed, ResourceWarning 32 -> 0 (3 benign third-party Starlette/statsmodels warnings remain, out of scope). ruff clean. Workflow wf_859b542b-2c3.

title: Deferred low-priority hardening from FastAPI review
description:
Intentionally deferred during the lyo9 remediation (2026-06-21) — low value and/or cross-cutting risk. Pick up opportunistically:
- lazy="raise" on Event.field_values/meta_values/tags/event_type (models/event.py) — fail-fast on implicit async lazy loads. Deferred: requires auditing many call sites.
- PUT /settings and PUT /settings/ai (api/v1/app_settings.py) currently delegate to PATCH. Either implement true replace-all semantics or drop the PUT alias. Deferred: check frontend usage first (risk of breaking the UI).
- Settings frozen=True (config.py) + convert direct settings mutations in tests (conftest.py, test_app_settings.py, test_security_middleware.py) to monkeypatch.setattr. Deferred: touches multiple test files owned by different change-lanes.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-06-21 after close inspection of each item:

ITEM 2 (PUT/PATCH settings) — DONE. Added docstrings to put_service_settings and put_ai_settings documenting intentional upsert/partial semantics. Removal was NOT viable: the frontend (frontend/src/api/serviceSettings.ts:13) calls PUT /settings/ai, so the route must stay; 'true replace-all' would break the UI's partial-save form.

ITEM 3 (frozen Settings / test isolation) — DONE (corrected). Converted the two uncoupled rate_limit_trust_forwarded_for tests in test_security_middleware.py to monkeypatch.setattr (guaranteed restore even on assert failure). Did NOT add Settings frozen=True: it is INCOMPATIBLE with monkeypatch.setattr (frozen pydantic models reject __setattr__ — i.e. it would break the finding's own suggested mechanism), and grep confirms no runtime code mutates settings (only tests did). Left test_app_settings.py:19-76 on try/finally because that mutation is coupled to crypto._fernet.cache_clear() which monkeypatch cannot re-run on teardown; conftest.py:12 left as the intentional suite-wide rate-limit default.

ITEM 1 (lazy='raise' on Event relations) — WON'T DO (deliberate). The 4 Event relations are already lazy='selectin' (always eager), so the MissingGreenlet/implicit-lazy-load bug the finding feared CANNOT occur today. Converting to lazy='raise' has a ~16 source-file + 7 test-file blast radius, requires adding explicit selectinload at every Event load site, and risks runtime 500s on any path not covered by the 540-test suite — a bad trade on a live self-hosted app for a marginal anti-over-fetch gain (over-fetch is batched, not N+1). Violates KISS/YAGNI. Kept selectin. Re-open as a dedicated perf task only if Event over-fetch is ever measured as a real bottleneck.
close_reason: Item 2 (PUT docstrings) + item 3 (monkeypatch test isolation) done & green; item 1 (lazy=raise) deliberately not done — already-selectin-safe, 16-file blast radius, YAGNI/regression risk. Rationale in notes.

title: Data-access & code-hygiene cleanups (dialect resolution, N+1, schema config, settings semantics)
description:
LOW — assorted, low-risk cleanups (async/data-access + routers reviewers):
- Resolve SQL dialect once at startup instead of per-request `session.get_bind().dialect.name` on an AsyncSession (`_search_query.py:49`, also worker/search_reindex.py:19, worker/tasks/metrics/schedule.py:53) — `get_bind()` on AsyncSession is deprecated/fragile in SQLAlchemy 2.x and the engine never changes at runtime. Use `session.bind.dialect.name` or inject a startup-resolved boolean.
- `bulk_create_events` field validation (event_service.py:572) issues one SELECT FieldDefinition per unique event type — replace with a single `WHERE event_type_id IN (...)` + Python groupby.
- `AlertDestinationResponse`/`AlertRuleResponse` (schemas/alerting.py:398,133) lack `model_config = {"from_attributes": True}` — add for consistency / future model_validate safety.
- `PUT /settings` and `PUT /settings/ai` (app_settings.py:65,82) just delegate to PATCH (partial-update under PUT is surprising) — either implement true replace semantics or drop the PUT alias.
- (Optional hardening) Add `lazy="raise"` to `Event.field_values/meta_values/tags/event_type` to fail-fast on implicit async lazy loads; fix resulting call sites with explicit selectinload.
- `_search_query.py:104,200` interpolate a constant `type_clause` into `text()` — currently safe (hardcoded), but refactor to always-bind params (`WHERE 1=0` guard) to keep the pattern injection-proof.
close_reason: Done (partial): dialect sniff via session.bind, bulk_create_events N+1 -> single IN query, type_clause now bound params, from_attributes on alerting responses. DEFERRED lazy=raise + PUT/PATCH (see follow-up). Green.

title: OpenAPI quality: tags, servers, error response models, explicit status codes, concrete return types
description:
LOW/MEDIUM — OpenAPI hygiene (app-core + routers reviewers). The generated spec is thin:
- `FastAPI(...)` (main.py:41-46) sets only title/version/description — no `openapi_tags` (so Swagger groups routes under raw tag strings with no descriptions) and no `servers` (breaks "Try it out" in non-default deployments). Add both (servers from settings.app_base_url).
- No route declares `responses={401|403|404|422: {model: ErrorDetail}}`, and there is essentially no `summary=`/`description=` on routes. Define a shared `ErrorDetail` schema (`detail: str`) and attach the relevant error responses + summaries to protected/externally-consumed routes.
- scans.py: all 12 handlers are typed `-> object:`, which defeats mypy response-body checking (runtime response_model still enforced). Replace with concrete schema types (ScanConfigResponse / ScanJobResponse / list[...]).
- auth.py:48 `POST /login` and other 200 routes: add explicit `status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK` for spec accuracy.
close_reason: Done: openapi_tags + servers, ErrorDetail schema (schemas/errors.py), scans.py concrete return types (no more -> object:), explicit login status_code. Green.

title: P5 — Events bulk-action bar: inactive-looking actions + wrapping label
description:
## P5 — Events bulk-action bar: inactive-looking actions + wrapping "Assign owner…"

**Defect (reported, Image #4):** the floating bulk-action bar ("N selected | Set status… | Mark
reviewed | Assign owner… | Delete selected | ×") reads as disabled — actions look greyed/inactive —
and "Assign owner…" wraps to two lines ("Assign / owner…").

### Root cause (`frontend/src/pages/events/BulkActionBar.tsx`)
The bar shell (38-44: fixed bottom-center, `bg var(--bg-elevated)`, `border var(--border-strong)`,
shadow-lg) is correct and matches the mockup. The problems are per-control:
- **Greyed look.** The two `Select` triggers ("Set status…" 49-64, "Assign owner…" 76-91) use the
  shadcn trigger base (`select.tsx:19`): `bg-transparent` + `data-[placeholder]:text-muted-foreground`
  + muted chevron. Since their value is always empty (placeholder), text + chevron both render at
  `--muted-foreground` → `--fg-subtle` ≈ oklch(0.52), genuinely low-contrast on the 0.17 bar. The
  "Delete selected" Button (93-102) is `variant="ghost"` + explicit `text-muted-foreground` at rest
  (greyed until hover). "Mark reviewed" (65-74) is `variant="ghost"` with no rest fill/border.
- **Wrapping.** Both Select triggers are pinned to fixed `w-32` (8rem). With `justify-between` + the
  chevron eating ~16px, "Assign owner…" (text-xs) doesn't fit on one line and wraps.

### Proposed fix (**zero deps**; edit ONLY `BulkActionBar.tsx`)
**Do NOT change `components/ui/button.tsx`, `button-variants.ts`, or `components/ui/select.tsx`** —
global primitives are tripl-1p25's scope and would regress other surfaces. All needed tokens
(`--danger`, `--danger-soft`, `--surface-hover`, `--border-strong`, `--fg`) already exist and are
exposed via `@theme`.

**A) Stop the wrapping** (both SelectTriggers, lines 54 & 81):
- Add `whitespace-nowrap`.
- Replace `w-32` with intrinsic sizing: `w-auto min-w-[8rem]` for "Set status…",
  `w-auto min-w-[9.5rem]` (~152px, fits "Assign owner…" + chevron at text-xs) for "Assign owner…".
  (A fixed `w-36`/`w-40` on the Assign trigger is an acceptable alternative.) Keep `h-7 text-xs`.
  → e.g. `className="h-7 w-auto min-w-[8rem] whitespace-nowrap text-xs"` (and `min-w-[9.5rem]` for Assign).

**B) Give every action a clearly-active affordance.** Recommended **B1** (raise contrast, keep
ghost/transparent — closest to the mockup's ghost-row bulk bar):
- Selects: lift placeholder + chevron contrast — `data-[placeholder]:text-foreground
  [&_svg]:text-foreground/70`; optionally add a visible edge via `border-[var(--border-strong)]`.
- "Mark reviewed": switch `variant="ghost"` → `variant="outline"` (visible 1px border + bg-background
  + hover surface), keep `size="sm" h-7 text-xs`.
- "Delete selected": remove the rest-state `text-muted-foreground`; use soft-danger so it's clearly
  active + destructive at rest: `className="h-7 text-xs text-[var(--danger)]
  hover:bg-[var(--danger-soft)] hover:text-[var(--danger)]"` (tokens at index.css:42-43,115-116,
  exposed 296-297).
- Keep the "×" clear button as-is (104-111).

Alternative **B2** (stronger "these are buttons" read): give each action a soft-filled pill
(`variant="outline"` or `bg-[var(--surface-hover)]` rest) + the B1 placeholder fix. Busier bar;
matches the compact dense-UI preference. **Pick B1 or B2 before coding.**

**C) Preserve disabled semantics:** the existing `disabled={disabled}` (driven by
isDeleting/isUpdating) keeps `opacity-50` — ensure new active styles are opacity-1 at rest so
enabled vs in-flight states stay distinguishable.

**Cross-ref tripl-1p25:** when that lands an `xs` size + soft `danger` variant in button-variants.ts,
migrate this bar's Delete → `variant="danger" size="xs"` and the ghost actions → `size="xs"` for the
denser mockup rhythm. For now do the local className fix to avoid the cross-surface regression
tripl-1p25 warns about.

### Acceptance criteria
- Dark theme, rows selected: "Set status…"/"Assign owner…" placeholders + chevrons render at readable
  (foreground-level) contrast — no longer look disabled.
- "Mark reviewed" + "Delete selected" have a visible at-rest affordance (border or non-muted/colored
  text); "Delete selected" reads as destructive (red) at rest, not only on hover.
- "Assign owner…" renders on a **single line** at the default bar width (no "Assign / owner…" wrap).
- While a bulk mutation is in flight, controls still dim (`disabled:opacity-50`) — enabled vs disabled
  stays distinguishable.
- **No** changes to button.tsx / button-variants.ts / select.tsx (global primitives untouched). No new dep.
- `pnpm lint` (zero warnings), `pnpm test` (EventsPage.test.tsx "Set status" combobox + "Delete
  selected" assertions still pass — keep aria-labels + visible text), `pnpm build` pass.

### Open questions
- **B1 vs B2** design choice — recommend B1 + danger-soft Delete; confirm with design owner. (Compact
  dense-UI preference could argue B2.) Settle before coding to avoid a rework cycle.
- Should "Set status"/"Assign owner" become icon+ghost menu buttons (short labels, no width problem)
  rather than inline w-32 Selects? Larger UX change — out of scope unless requested.
- Wait for tripl-1p25's xs/danger variant then refactor, vs ship the local fix now (recommend now).

**Risk:** Low — isolated presentational change in one component using className/variant swaps +
existing tokens. Keep aria-label "Set status"/"Assign owner" + visible "Delete selected" text for the
tests (EventsPage.test.tsx:395,467-468). Spot-check light mode. Shares EventsPage.test.tsx surface
with P3 — whoever lands second re-runs the file.
close_reason: Closed

title: P3 — Inline Events table: right-edge overflow + restyle native status selector
description:
## P3 — Inline Events table: right-edge overflow/scroll + restyle native status selector

**Defect (reported, Image #3):** on the event-type detail "Events" tab the table looks broken on the
right: (1) the vertical scrollbar is detached from the table frame; (2) row data bleeds past the
right delimiter; (3) changing status shows an "ugly popup with a name"; (4) the status selector
("Live" dropdown) is unstyled/ugly.

Context: the Events tab embeds the real Events table via `<EventsPage lockType embedded />`
(`EventTypeDetailView.tsx:129`); the same components back the standalone Events list.

### Root cause
1. **Right-edge frame:** `.tripl-table-wrap` (`index.css:148-155`) draws only **top+bottom** borders
   — no left/right frame. The scroll wrapper (`overflowY:auto`, EventsTable.tsx:164-173) thus has no
   visible right border, and the sticky `right-0` actions column's `border-l` becomes the only
   vertical line near the edge, so the hover actions overlay (`EventRowActions`, positioned over a
   thin sticky cell, extending left with `pr-3`) reads as content bleeding past the edge. The footer
   bar (EventsTable.tsx:361-389) has only `border-t`, breaking the frame further.
   - **`.tripl-table-wrap` is single-use** (only `EventsTable.tsx:166`) — confirmed by grep, so this
     is safely scoped to the events table.
2. **Status selector:** `EventRowActions.tsx` uses a **raw native `<select>`/`<option>`** (lines
   66-79) instead of the shadcn `Select` primitive used elsewhere (cf. `BulkActionBar.tsx:49-64`).
   Native select renders the OS option popup ("ugly popup with a name") and can't be themed. The
   reorder up/down buttons + select carry `title` attributes (lines 46,57,71) → native OS tooltips.

### Proposed fix (**zero deps** — radix select/tooltip already present)

**Fix 1 — continuous frame + aligned scrollbar.** Recommended: wrap table+footer in **one**
bordered/rounded container in `EventsPage.tsx` (around the EventsTable at ~338-385) — e.g.
`<div className="rounded-[10px] border overflow-hidden" style={{ borderColor: 'var(--border)' }}>` —
and drop the redundant top/bottom-only borders from `.tripl-table-wrap`. This frames scroll-area +
footer continuously in both embedded and standalone modes. Keep `overflow-x/-y:auto` on the inner
scroll wrapper (don't `overflow:hidden` the scroller). Verify the sticky trailing actions
header/cell backgrounds (`bg-[var(--bg-sunken)]` EventsTable.tsx:283; `bg-background` EventRow.tsx:327)
still mask scrolled content, and sticky-header z-index still works with the new wrapper.

**Fix 2 — restyle inline status editor to shadcn Select + Chip/Dot** (rewrite
`EventRowActions.tsx:64-84`): replace native select with `Select/SelectTrigger/SelectValue/
SelectContent/SelectItem` from `@/components/ui/select` (already used by BulkActionBar). Compact
trigger mirroring BulkActionBar: `<SelectTrigger className="h-6 w-auto gap-1 px-2 text-[11px]"
aria-label="Set event status">`. Render the value as a status `Chip` (tone via
`EVENT_STATUS_TONE`) and each option with a leading `Dot` (`EVENT_STATUS_DOT_TONE`), reusing
`lib/eventStatus.ts` (LABELS/TONE/DOT_TONE) + `EVENT_STATUSES` to match the read-only EventRow chip
(`EventRow.tsx:173-179`). Wire `value={event.status}` + `onValueChange={(v)=>onSetStatus?.(v as
EventStatus)}`. Drop the manual `ChevronDown` (lines 80-82, import line 2).
**CRITICAL:** keep `aria-label="Set event status"` exactly — `EventsPage.test.tsx:223` asserts
`getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Set event status' })`, and the Radix trigger is also
`role="combobox"`, so the test passes only if the accessible name is preserved.

**Fix 3 — kill native tooltips.** Remove the `title` attrs on the reorder buttons
(`EventRowActions.tsx:46,57`); keep `aria-label` (tests assert names "Move event up"/"Move event
down"). Optionally wrap in shadcn `Tooltip` (a `TooltipProvider` is already mounted at
`EventsTable.tsx:161`) — or just drop `title` and rely on aria-label. Either satisfies "no ugly popup".

**Portal note:** the editor lives inside a `pointer-events-none` hover overlay
(`EventRowActions.tsx:35` `focus-within:flex`, children `pointer-events-auto`). Radix Select content
portals to body, so it isn't clipped by table `overflow`; verify the row stays visible while the
dropdown is open (focus-within should hold it) — **this needs real-browser interaction QA**, jsdom
can't prove it.

### Acceptance criteria
- Both standalone EventsPage and the embedded type-detail Events tab show a continuous border on all
  four sides; the vertical scrollbar sits inside the frame, flush with a visible right border.
- Row content + hover actions overlay no longer bleed past the right edge; the sticky trailing cell
  renders inside the right border and masks scrolled content.
- Clicking the row status control opens a **themed shadcn** dropdown (dark surface, teal accent,
  Chip+Dot per status) — no OS-native option popup; the trigger itself is a compact styled control,
  not a raw native box.
- Hovering reorder buttons / status control shows **no** native tooltip; accessible names preserved.
- `pnpm test` green — specifically `getByRole('combobox',{name:'Set event status'})` and the
  "Move event up"/"Move event down" queries still resolve.
- `pnpm lint` (zero warnings) + `pnpm build` pass. No new dependency.

### Open questions
- Frame placement: EventsPage wrapper div (recommended — encloses footer) vs editing
  `.tripl-table-wrap` directly. Decide before coding.
- Trigger value as Chip (matches read-only EventRow) vs plain text+dot — confirm against
  `design/tripl/`.
- Full shadcn Tooltip on reorder buttons vs simply dropping `title`.

**Risk:** Medium — portal'd Radix Select inside a `pointer-events-none` hover overlay needs
real-browser QA. Test risk: preserve the `aria-label` accessible names or `EventsPage.test.tsx`
breaks. **Depends on P1** (verify the frame at full width). Shares `EventsPage.test.tsx` surface with
P5 — whoever lands second must re-run the full file.
close_reason: Closed

description:

Mockup Btn (design/tripl/project/primitives.jsx): variants primary/secondary/ghost/outline/danger; sizes xs/sm/md = h 22/28/32; icon-only square at sm = 28x28; active state for toggles.
Repo Button (components/ui/button.tsx + button-variants.ts): variants default/destructive/outline/secondary/ghost/link; sizes default/sm/lg/icon = h 36/32/40, icon = 36; ghost/outline already have active: states.

Gaps: no xs size; heights 36/32/40 vs 22/28/32; icon 36 vs 28; no dedicated 'danger' soft variant (has solid 'destructive').

Decide: tighten shadcn size scale to mockup heights (risk: visual regression across all pages already using Button, incl. f7q6.2 sidebar) vs accept shadcn scale as canonical and only add an xs size + danger-soft where surfaces need it. Recommend the latter (KISS, no regression). Revisit per surface task if a screen needs the denser mockup buttons.
close_reason: Closed

title: Investigate useEventRowMetrics full-set refetch growth with infinite scroll
description: src/pages/events/useEventRowMetrics.ts:38: window-metrics query key is the sorted/joined list of ALL visible event ids. With 200-row pages and infinite scroll every page append changes the key and refetches metrics for the entire accumulated set, and the 60s refetchInterval re-pulls all of them. close_reason: useEventRowMetrics window-metrics request is now bounded via id buckets so infinite-scroll page appends no longer re-key and refetch the entire accumulated set (and the 60s interval no longer re-pulls everything). Displayed data preserved; build/lint/test green.

title: Distribution drift detector (KS-test / PSI) on event field values
description: Catch 'composition changed' shifts that pure volume anomaly detection misses (e.g. 80% of events suddenly come from one platform). Add a new detector that, per scan window, samples value distributions for nominated low-cardinality fields and compares against a baseline window using PSI or two-sample KS. New model DistributionDrift (event_type_id, field_definition_id, bucket, statistic, p_value, baseline_summary, current_summary). Surface as a new alert candidate type and a 'Distribution' tab on MonitoringDetailPage. ScanConfig gains a 'distribution_drift_fields' selector. Worker: new analyzer module under worker/analyzers/distribution_drift.py reading via the existing warehouse adapters.
notes: Phase 1 done: compute_psi analyzer in worker/analyzers/distribution_drift.py (PSI score + stable/minor/significant band + top-N value contributions, epsilon-protected log/division), DistributionDrift model + Alembic migration d6e5f4a3b2c1, 6 unit tests. Phase 2 (open): (1) ScanConfig.distribution_drift_fields config column + UI; (2) worker scan/metrics task samples baseline-vs-current value distributions per configured field per bucket and writes DistributionDrift rows; (3) AlertMatchCandidate variant for band==significant rows so alert rules can opt-in; (4) MonitoringDetailPage 'Distribution' tab showing proportions chart + per-top-mover contribution breakdown.
close_reason: Completed Phase 2: added distribution_drift_fields config and migration, worker PSI persistence, distribution alert opt-in/candidates, API response, Monitoring Distribution tab, and focused backend/frontend coverage.

Wire-up: middleware in main.py for FastAPI, signals in celery_app.py for Celery. Env-gated so dev path stays quiet.

Counters wired from worker tasks: scan_runs_total (run_scan completed/failed), anomalies_detected_total{scope,direction} (_replace_scope_anomalies + _replace_scope_breakdown_anomalies), alert_deliveries_total{status} (alerts.send_alert_delivery sent/failed), schema_drifts_detected_total{drift_type} (_record_drift_metrics helper, both sqlite and pg upsert paths). title: P4 — Syntax-highlighting + Format SQL editor for scan Base query
description:
## P4 — Syntax-highlighting + Format SQL editor for the scan "Base query"

**Defect (reported):** «на странице редактирования скл для скана хотелось бы красивый редактор,
который поддерживает форматирование» — the scan SQL-editing field should be a nice editor with
syntax highlighting + formatting.

> NOTE: this is an **enhancement beyond the mockup** — `design/tripl/project/surface-pages.jsx:858`
> uses a plain mono `<TextArea>` for editing and a read-only `<pre className="mono">` (805) for
> display. And it is the **only** task in this epic that adds new dependencies. Gate on bundle-budget
> sign-off before starting.

### Current behavior
The "Base query" control is a plain shadcn `Textarea` (`font-mono text-sm`, rows=4, placeholder
"SELECT * FROM analytics.events"), rendered by **`SourceQuerySection`**
(`frontend/src/pages/settings/scans/ScanFormSections.tsx:73-81`), reading `state.baseQuery` /
writing via `setBaseQuery` (useScanForm). The SAME section is used by **both** the New-scan page
(`ScanConfigForm.tsx:223`) and the per-scan Configuration tab (`ScanConfigForm.tsx:110`) → one swap
covers create + edit. No highlighting, no formatting, no line numbers.

Precedent to mirror: `frontend/src/pages/events/JsonEditor.tsx` wraps a Textarea in a `relative` div
and overlays a ghost "Format" Button (`absolute right-1.5 top-1.5 h-6 text-[10px]`, lines 168-176)
that pretty-prints and routes the result back through `onChange` with a silent try/catch.

`frontend/package.json` confirms **zero** relevant deps (no codemirror/@codemirror/*,
@uiw/react-codemirror, monaco, prismjs, react-simple-code-editor, sql-formatter).

### Proposed fix
**Recommended stack:** `@uiw/react-codemirror` + `@codemirror/lang-sql` + `sql-formatter`
(`pnpm add @uiw/react-codemirror @codemirror/lang-sql sql-formatter` — **pnpm only**). CodeMirror 6
is tree-shaken/modular (~120-180KB min, ~45-60KB gzip), Vite-native ESM, no worker plumbing —
the sweet spot vs Monaco (multi-MB + worker config). Lighter **fallback**: `react-simple-code-editor`
+ `prismjs` (+ prism-sql) + `sql-formatter` (~10-15KB gzip, weaker editing fidelity).

Implementation (one new component + one swap; mirror JsonEditor):
1. New `frontend/src/pages/settings/scans/SqlEditor.tsx` exporting
   `SqlEditor({ value, onChange, placeholder?, minHeight? })`. Render `<CodeMirror>` with
   `extensions={[sql()]}`, `value`, `onChange`, `basicSetup={{ lineNumbers: true, foldGutter: false,
   highlightActiveLine: false }}`, wrapped in a `relative` div (for the Format overlay).
2. **Theme to design tokens** via a scoped `.cm-*` CSS block in `index.css` (so light mode `:root`
   AND the 6 accent variants at index.css:126-139 work — do NOT hardcode oklch): background
   `var(--bg-sunken)` (matches the read-only `<pre>` at surface-pages.jsx:805), border
   `var(--border-subtle)`, fg `var(--fg)`, caret/selection `var(--accent)` (teal), gutter
   `var(--fg-faint)`, font `var(--font-mono)` (JetBrains Mono), 13px. Match the Textarea frame:
   rounded-md, 1px border, teal focus ring.
3. **Format button:** overlay a ghost Button identical to JsonEditor.tsx:168-176; onClick runs
   `format(value, { language: 'sql' })` (sql-formatter) in try/catch (on failure keep text), pushing
   the result through the **same onChange**.
4. **Wire into form state** (`ScanFormSections.tsx`): replace the Textarea (74-80) with
   `<SqlEditor value={state.baseQuery} onChange={setBaseQuery} placeholder="SELECT * FROM analytics.events" />`.
   **CRITICAL:** route everything (incl. Format) through `setBaseQuery` (`useScanForm.ts:181-184`),
   which resets `jsonValuePaths` + preview-derived state on every change — bypassing it would leave a
   stale preview. Validation unchanged (Create/Preview gate on `state.baseQuery.trim()`,
   ScanFormSections.tsx:94 / ScanConfigForm.tsx:194). Remove the now-unused `Textarea` import
   (ScanFormSections.tsx:5).
5. **Tests:** `ScansTab.test.tsx:104` asserts `getByText('SELECT * FROM analytics.events_v2')`;
   CodeMirror tokenizes text across spans → switch to a substring/regex matcher or query the editor
   value container (add `data-testid`). `ScanDetail.test.tsx:119` only checks the "Source & query"
   heading — unaffected. If CodeMirror is flaky under jsdom layout measurement, stub it in tests.

### Acceptance criteria
- Base query in **both** New-scan and Configuration tab renders SQL with syntax highlighting
  (keywords/strings/identifiers visually distinct).
- A visible "Format" affordance pretty-prints via sql-formatter; malformed SQL is left unchanged (no crash).
- Editor bg/border/fg/caret follow design tokens in dark mode AND render correctly in light mode +
  accent variants.
- Typing + Format both update `state.baseQuery` through `setBaseQuery` (preview-derived state still
  resets on edit); Create/Preview still gated on non-empty trimmed base_query.
- `pnpm lint` (zero warnings), `pnpm test` (ScansTab.test.tsx text assertion updated), `pnpm build` pass.
- Any new dep added with **pnpm** (pnpm-lock.yaml updated), not npm/yarn.

### Open questions / decisions (resolve before coding)
- **Bundle budget sign-off:** is ~45-60KB gzip acceptable, or lazy-load the editor (`React.lazy`,
  only on scan create/edit), or take the lighter prismjs fallback? **Blocking decision.**
- **SQL dialect:** warehouses are ClickHouse/Postgres/BigQuery (cf. scanLayout.tsx `DB_HUE`). Generic
  'sql' is safe, but keying dialect off the selected data source's `db_type` highlights/formats more
  accurately — would add a `dialect` prop to SqlEditor.
- Should highlighting also drive the read-only base_query display (the `<pre>` at surface-pages.jsx:805)?
- Line numbers / fold gutter, or a minimal look closer to the current 4-row Textarea height?

**Risk:** Low-to-Medium — UI swap is low risk (one shared component, form wiring unchanged). Medium
because: new ~45-60KB dep; CodeMirror layout-measures under jsdom (may need a test stub + the
ScansTab assertion update); theming must cover light mode + accent variants (use CSS vars, not
hardcoded oklch).
